title: Eliminate the memory bloat (second copy of the factory + 8K render target + precomputed caches + leaks)

designs.problem: Eliminate Cartograph memory bloat: a full second copy of the factory in RAM, an 8K render target, precomputed per building caches, and an unbounded redirector leak.
designs.designName: Stable ID quadtree plus on demand caches plus scissored clear
designs.lens: Minimal diff, surgical fixes that keep the data driven CPU rasterization architecture but remove the worst leaks, the O(N) and O(N squared) bookkeeping, and the fixed VRAM and clear cost. No SceneCapture rewrite, no tiling subsystem, no new replication protocol. Every change is local to existing functions and independently shippable.
designs.approach:
PROBLEM RESTATED. CurrentBuildingData (CartographGameInstanceModule.h:359) is a TArray of FBuildingData, one heavyweight record per buildable, roughly 344 to 432 bytes each including precomputed screen space caches. Alongside it sit BuildingDataIndexRedirector (h:365, a never shrinking int32 array that leaks 4 bytes per lifetime placement, documented at h:361 to 364) and CurrentBuildingQuadTree (h:366, a TQuadTree of int32 storing positional array indices). An 8192 by 8192 RGBA8 render target costs a fixed 256 MB VRAM, and every redraw issues a full size opaque clear tile (cpp:653 to 660).

The root cause of the redirector leak, the per event O(N) scans, and the O(N squared) initial load is one design decision: the quadtree stores positional indices into a Z sorted array, so insert and remove renumber everything, and the redirector exists only to patch that up. Break that coupling and four problems collapse at once.

CHANGE 1, stable IDs in the quadtree, delete the redirector. Add a uint32 Id field to FBuildingData (plus 4 bytes, dwarfed by what is removed) and a monotonic NextBuildingId counter. Change TQuadTree of int32 to TQuadTree of uint32 keyed by the stable id. TQuadTree Remove matches by element equality, which works correctly now because the id never changes; the old positional int is exactly why the redirector workaround was needed. OnBuildingDataAdd (cpp:1194) assigns the id, calls Insert with id and box, and the reindex loop at cpp:1199 to 1205 is deleted, taking it from O(N) to O(log N). OnBuildingDataRemove (cpp:1213) deletes the full scan at cpp:1217 to 1230 and calls Remove with id and box directly, also O(N) to O(log N). The Z sorted array still shifts on insert and remove, so rebuild a TMap of uint32 to int32 IdToIndex once per redraw pass, O(N) once per redraw, not per event, to translate quadtree ids back to array indices in the read path at cpp:686 to 692. This is strictly cheaper than today, which pays O(N) per event inside the cancellation guard at cpp:562. The initial gather at cpp:522 to 526 becomes O(N log N) for free because OnBuildingDataAdd no longer scans; the old reindex there was provably always false anyway since the array is pre sorted (cpp:520) and processed in increasing order. Follow up Step 1.5, larger diff, deferred under the lens: move CurrentBuildingData to a TSparseArray with a separate Z index to also remove the O(N) memmove at cpp:575 and cpp:597, but ship Step 1 first since it already removes the leak and the quadratic load.

CHANGE 2, drop precomputed screen space caches from the resident record. FNormalDataCache (CartographDataStructure.h:60 to 66) stores ScreenPosition, Size, Rotation, and Corners of 4 (about 152 bytes, the Corners live in FRectangleDataCache at h:53 to 57) that are pure functions of Transform plus per class data. Recompute them in the draw loop at cpp:714 and onward from Transform plus a per class lookup keyed by classHash; keep only classHash, Transform, and VisualBoxCache for culling. This shrinks FBuildingData from about 344 to 432 bytes down to about 180 to 200 bytes. It also removes duplicated corner math, since FillInCache (CartographDataStructure.cpp:423 to 433) and FillInVisualBoxCache (cpp:526 to 540) currently compute the same four corners twice on the build hot path.

CHANGE 3, quarter the VRAM and shrink the clear. Set RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE to 1024 times 4 (header line 35) and re author the uasset SizeX and SizeY to 4096, taking VRAM from 256 MB to 64 MB. ORIGIN_UV and PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER are constexpr derived from the size (h:37 to 38) so the code stays self consistent; only the uasset must match. For partial redraws, size the ClearItem to the already computed scissor bounds MinIntX through MaxIntY (cpp:641 to 645) instead of the full screen (cpp:653 to 657), cutting per event clear bandwidth by orders of magnitude for localized edits.

The three changes are orthogonal and independently shippable. Change 1 is highest ROI and lowest risk because it deletes a documented hack. Change 3 is near one line plus an asset edit. Change 2 is the biggest per building memory win but touches the draw loop, so ship it last.

Issue mapping: issue 14 lag spikes, leak, and TDR from Change 1 (O(log N), leak gone) plus Change 3 (smaller clear and VRAM). Issue 10 localized and budgeted redraw from the Change 3 scissored clear. The general memory complaint from all three. Issue 9 server join crash eased by Change 1 cutting server side O(N squared) ingestion during concurrent joins.
designs.complexityBefore: Per event: O(N) redirector scan, plus O(N) Z sorted Insert or RemoveAt memmove, plus O(N) linear remove match scan (cpp:587 to 605), three O(N) operations where N grows with lifetime placements because the redirector never shrinks. Initial gather O(N squared) (cpp:522 to 526). Memory about 344 to 432 bytes per building resident, plus 4 bytes per building leaked redirector, plus about 48 bytes per building quadtree box, plus 256 MB VRAM. A full 8192 by 8192 opaque clear tile is submitted every redraw.
designs.complexityAfter: Per event: O(log N) quadtree insert or remove, plus the O(N) Z sorted memmove unchanged until Step 1.5. The redirector scan is eliminated, and N is now live count, not lifetime. Initial gather O(N log N). Memory about 180 to 200 bytes per building resident, 0 leaked redirector, per class tables bounded by a few hundred classes, and 64 MB VRAM. Clear tile sized to the scissor, a few hundred pixels for a single belt instead of 67 million texels.
dataStructures: TQuadTree of uint32 keyed by stable id (was TQuadTree of int32), with Remove now correct because the id is immutable
uint32 NextBuildingId monotonic counter, or a TSparseArray slot index used as the id later to drop the separate counter
TMap of uint32 to int32 IdToIndex, rebuilt once per redraw pass rather than per event
TArray of FBuildingData, same container but the record shrinks about 2x once derived caches are dropped; optionally TSparseArray of FBuildingData later for O(1) stable slot add and remove
TMap of uint32 to FPerClassDrawData, per class draw data (category color, size override, layer pointer, spline data) looked up once at draw time by classHash instead of stored per building
DELETED: TArray of int32 BuildingDataIndexRedirector, both the leak and the O(N) scans
designs.memoryImpact: Per building resident drops from about 344 to 432 bytes down to about 180 to 200 bytes after Change 2, roughly half. The redirector leak is eliminated; it was an unbounded plus 4 bytes per lifetime placement. At 200k live buildings the array drops from about 69 MB to about 38 MB, and a session that churned a million placements stops leaking the proportional tombstones plus quadtree element bloat. VRAM goes from 256 MB to 64 MB (Change 3), a 192 MB reduction, the single largest fixed memory win. Net: roughly 50 percent per building RAM reduction, the unbounded leak removed, and 192 MB VRAM saved.
risks: TQuadTree Remove matches by element equality on the id, so ids must never be reused within a session. A monotonic uint32 wrapping at 4.29 billion placements is effectively unreachable in a play session; use uint64 if paranoid. Verify the UE5.3 Remove signature is Remove of const ElementType ref and const FBox2D ref before deleting the redirector.

Change 2 recompute must exactly reproduce FillInCache math (world_position_to_screen_position at cpp:387, corner TransformPosition at cpp:423 to 433) or icons and rectangles shift. Mitigate by extracting a shared pure helper called both ways during a transition, then deleting the stored fields once verified pixel identical.

Async icon load mid draw (cpp:755 to 758) relies on a cached soft pointer in FNormalDataCache. Pre resolve and pin the distinct icon textures before BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (cpp:630) so the draw loop never co awaits AsyncLoadObject during the open canvas pass.

Resizing RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE requires re authoring the uasset SizeX and SizeY to 4096 in editor, or the map scales wrong. Transforms are constexpr derived so the code stays consistent, but the asset must match.
4096 halves linear resolution to about 2.18 cm per pixel on a 7.5 km world, still far finer than a minimap needs; verify icon legibility at max zoom or expose the size as a config option.

Step 1.5 TSparseArray plus separate Z index is a larger diff. If deferred, the O(N) Z sorted Insert and RemoveAt memmove remains as the residual per event cost, still a major improvement over today three O(N) plus the leak, but not the full O(log N) ideal.

The lazy IdToIndex rebuild is O(N) per redraw pass. That is fine for full redraws which are already O(N), but a localized single belt redraw must map only the small GetElements result set, not the full N, or the localized path regains an O(N) term.
implementationSketch: 1a, CartographDataStructure.h:75 to 109: add uint32 Id to FBuildingData; exclude it from NetSerialize and operator equals since it is host local identity, clients assign fresh ids on their own add path.
1b, CartographGameInstanceModule.h:359 to 366: change TQuadTree of int32 to TQuadTree of uint32; delete BuildingDataIndexRedirector; add uint32 NextBuildingId and TMap of uint32 to int32 IdToIndex.
1c, cpp:1194 to 1210 OnBuildingDataAdd: set Id equal to NextBuildingId post increment, make the parameter mutable, call Insert with Id and VisualBoxCache, delete the reindex loop at cpp:1199 to 1205.
1d, cpp:1213 to 1234 OnBuildingDataRemove: delete the full scan at cpp:1217 to 1230, call Remove with the building Id and VisualBoxCache directly.

1e, cpp:686 to 692 read path: GetElements fills a TArray of uint32; rebuild IdToIndex once at the top of the localized branch, map id to index, then keep the existing Algo Sort and Min and Max Z trim at cpp:693 to 708; remove the dead redirector deref at cpp:691.
1f, cpp:468 and cpp:520 to 526 InitialBuildableGather: drop BuildingDataIndexRedirector.Empty(); the add loop is unchanged in shape but is now O(N log N) because OnBuildingDataAdd is O(log N).

2a, CartographDataStructure.cpp FillInCache:264 to 446: extract the geometry math ScreenPosition, Corners, Size, Rotation into a pure ComputeDrawGeometry helper used by the draw loop instead of reading stored FNormalDataCache.

2b, build a TMap of uint32 to FPerClassDrawData once from BuildableSizeOverrideMap and BuildCategoryDataMap, looked up by classHash at draw time; drop the stored FNormalDataCache and FRectangleDataCache geometry.
2c, pre resolve and pin the distinct icon textures before BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget at cpp:630 so the draw loop never suspends on AsyncLoadObject at cpp:755 to 758.
3a, CartographGameInstanceModule.h:35: RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE equals 1024 times 4.
3b, re author Content UI CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization.uasset SizeX and SizeY to 4096 in editor.

3c, cpp:653 to 660: on the partial non entire branch, build ClearItem at position MinIntX MinIntY with size MaxIntX minus MinIntX by MaxIntY minus MinIntY from the already computed scissor bounds at cpp:641 to 645, instead of zero zero to RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE.

Validation: build; load a large base save and confirm pixel identical render after Change 2; run a long build and dismantle session and confirm flat memory via stat memory after Change 1; confirm VRAM drop via GPU stats after Change 3; profile OnBuildingDataAdd to confirm a single belt placement no longer scans the full array.

designs.problem: Cartograph maintains a full second copy of the entire factory (CurrentBuildingData: TArray<FBuildingData>, ~344-368 B/building, CartographGameInstanceModule.h:359) plus a TQuadTree<int32> + never-shrinking BuildingDataIndexRedirector (h:365-366), a permanently-resident 8192x8192 RGBA8 render target (256 MB VRAM, h:35), and per-building precomputed screen-space caches (FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache, ~152-192 B of which is trivially recomputable, DataStructure.h:60-66). At 1M buildings this is ~360 MB of duplicated heap + 256 MB VRAM. The redirector leaks monotonically (tombstoned -1 on remove at cpp:1224, never compacted) and forces O(N) scans on every single add (cpp:1199-1205) and remove (cpp:1217-1230), making initial load O(N^2) and per-event ingestion O(N). This drives the high-memory complaint, the 15s lag spikes (#14), and contributes to the join-time server memory pressure (#9).
designs.designName: Engine-as-truth + slim deltas: drop the parallel factory copy, store a stable-handle slim record only where the engine can't, and recompute draw geometry on demand against a uniform spatial grid and per-class lookup table
designs.lens: Best-end-state redesign of the data model and rendering even if larger; optimize for correctness and scaling to million-building factories.
designs.approach:
The root cause is that Cartograph treats itself as a second authoritative store of the factory and pre-bakes per-building render state into that store. Every other problem (O(N^2) load, O(N) per-event, redirector leak, memory bloat) follows from coupling identity to array position, coupling Z-filter to storage order, and caching derived data per-building. The end-state design breaks all three couplings.

(1) STORAGE MODEL — split into "what is non-derivable" vs "what is derivable", and key everything by a STABLE HANDLE, never an array position.

  Replace `TArray<FBuildingData> CurrentBuildingData` + `TArray<int32> BuildingDataIndexRedirector` + `TQuadTree<int32>` with:
   - `TSparseArray<FSlimBuildingRecord> Records` — the master store. A slot index is the building's stable BuildingId (TSparseArray gives O(1) Add returning a stable index, O(1) RemoveAt, and reuses freed slots via its internal free list; positions never shift on insert/remove). Add a generation counter (`TArray<uint16> Generation` parallel to slots, bumped on free) if you want ABA-safe handles for the RCO/UI paths.
   - `FSlimBuildingRecord` = { uint32 ClassHash; FVector3f Position (12 B, single-precision is plenty for a 7.5km map at ~1cm/px); float YawRadians (4 B); EBuildingDataType Type:8; uint16 ExtraIndex } plus a side-table `TArray<FSplineExtraData> / TArray<FWireExtraData> / TArray<FBeamExtraData>` indexed by ExtraIndex ONLY for splines/wires/beams. Normal buildings (icons/rectangles — the vast majority of foundations/machines) carry zero extra data. Record size drops from ~344-368 B to ~24-28 B (12-15x). The full FTransform (quat+scale, 96 B) is gone: scale is already dropped on the wire (DataStructure.cpp:128-130) and the only rotation used at draw time is yaw (FRotator passed to FCanvasTileItem.Rotation at cpp:772/798 — pitch/roll are irrelevant for a top-down map), so store one float.
   - DELETE the DataCache variant entirely (FNormalDataCache 168 B / FRectangleDataCache 104 B / VisualBoxCache 40 B per building, ~152-192 B). All of it — ScreenPosition, Size, Corners[4], Rotation, the CategoryData/SplineData/WireData pointers, the layer pointer — is recomputed at draw time from ClassHash via a PER-CLASS table (see 3) and the record's Position/Yaw. FillInCache (DataStructure.cpp:264-446) and FillInVisualBoxCache become draw-time pure functions, not per-building stored state.

(2) SPATIAL INDEX — uniform hash grid keyed by stable BuildingId, replacing the quadtree+redirector.

  World bounds are fixed and known at compile time (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH_BOUND, h:28-31; ~7500m x 7500m). Use `TMap<FIntPoint, TArray<BuildingId>> Grid` (or, since bounds are fixed, a flat `TArray<TArray<BuildingId>>` of GRID_W*GRID_H cells) with cell size tuned to the typical building+expansion footprint (e.g. 50 m -> 150x150 = 22500 cells, ~bounded). On add: compute the building's visual AABB on the fly, insert BuildingId into each overlapped cell — O(cells overlapped) ~ O(1). On remove: erase BuildingId from those cells — O(1) (or store the cell list in the record). Box query for a dirty rect visits only overlapping cells. This makes add/remove O(1) instead of O(N), eliminates the redirector and its leak entirely, and removes the per-element 40 B FBox2D the quadtree stored. No node splitting, cache-friendly, bounded memory.

(3) Z-FILTER decoupled from storage — a separate Z-index so the master store needs NO ordering.

  Keep a `TArray<TPair<float, BuildingId>> ZIndex` sorted by Z, updated O(log N) per mutation (or coarse 1 m Z-bands: `TMap<int32, TArray<BuildingId>>` for O(1)). The height slider (OnZFilterUpdated, cpp:935) does a range-select on ZIndex; storage stays unordered and stable. This is the single design choice (Z-sorting the master array, used for Algo::LowerBound at cpp:573/584/663) that forced unstable positions and thus the redirector.

(4) PER-CLASS TABLE — `TMap<uint32, FClassDrawInfo> ClassDrawTable`, sized by number of buildable CLASSES (hundreds), not instances. FClassDrawInfo = { Size (after override), EBuildingDataType, const FCategoryData*, const FSplineData*, const FWireData*, const FBuildLayerData*, extra-rotation, icon soft ptr }. Built ONCE at GatherBuildables. The draw loop looks up ClassDrawTable[record.ClassHash] (one hash lookup) and computes ScreenPosition/Corners/Size from record.Position+Yaw+Size in a few FLOPs — exactly the work FillInCache did, but at draw time, not stored 1M times. This also removes the duplicated FillInCache/FillInVisualBoxCache corner-transform work (currently done twice, DataStructure.cpp:423-433 and 526-540).

(5) HOST optimization (optional, biggest memory win): on a listen/single-player host, the engine already holds the data (AFGBuildableSubsystem::GetAllBuildablesRef + AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem::mBuildableClassToInstanceArray, read at cpp:383-388). The host can DROP the Records store and iterate those engine arrays per dirty cell at draw time, keeping only the Grid (BuildingId -> a cheap reference into the engine arrays) + ZIndex. Only dedicated-server CLIENTS (which receive data via the RCO because they lack the subsystem data) need to keep the slim Records. This eliminates the second copy on the host entirely.

(6) RENDER TARGET — make RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE a config option defaulting to 4096 (64 MB VRAM, 4x less; the asset SizeX/SizeY must match). Keep partial_redraw's idea but fix the clear: replace the full-size 8192^2 opaque ClearItem (cpp:653-660) with a clear sized to ScissorArea bounds (the code already computes MinIntX/Y..MaxIntX/Y at cpp:641-645) so partial redraws only touch the dirty rect — orders-of-magnitude less per-event GPU bandwidth, directly attacking the #14 TDR. The cancel-restart thrash (RedrawMap Cancel at cpp:442 on every event) should be replaced by debounced dirty-rect accumulation: drain PendingAdd/Remove into the grid continuously (cheap O(1) ops now), and coalesce DRAW into at most one budgeted redraw per quiescence window, expanding a dirty-rect set instead of throwing away completed work.

This design resolves #14 (O(1) ingestion kills the 15s spikes and the leak; smaller/scissored clear + 4096 target attacks the GPU TDR), #10 (grid query gives true localized redraws + the debounced budget + an explicit full-redraw trigger), #9 (slim records + streaming RCO cut per-join server memory; see RCO note), and the high-memory complaint (12-15x smaller records, no derived cache, 4x smaller VRAM, no redirector leak).
designs.complexityBefore: Initial load: O(N^2) (InitialBuildableGather loops OnBuildingDataAdd over a growing redirector, cpp:522-526 x 1199-1205) and a by-value deep copy of the engine lightweight map (cpp:387,456). Per add: O(N) redirector scan + O(N) array Insert memmove. Per remove: O(N) Z-bucket linear scan (cpp:587-605) + O(N) redirector scan + O(N) RemoveAt. Mass dismantle of K: O(K*N). Memory: ~344-368 B/building heap (full second copy + ~152-192 B derived cache) + 256 MB VRAM + monotonically-leaking redirector (4 B per lifetime-add, never reclaimed) + 48 B/building quadtree element.
designs.complexityAfter: Initial load: O(N log N) (bulk insert into grid + build ZIndex; no per-element redirector rewrite, no by-value engine-map copy — iterate by const-ref). Per add: O(1) sparse-array slot + O(1) grid cell insert + O(log N) ZIndex insert (or O(1) with Z-bands). Per remove: O(1) sparse-array free + O(1) grid erase + O(log N) ZIndex. Mass dismantle of K: O(K log N). Dirty-rect draw: O(buildings in dirty cells). Memory: ~24-28 B/record (host: zero records, just grid+ZIndex referencing engine arrays) + per-class table O(classes) + 64 MB VRAM (at 4096) + grid cells (bounded by world, ~22500 cells) + no leak.

FSlimBuildingRecord { uint32 ClassHash; FVector3f Position; float YawRadians; EBuildingDataType Type; uint16 ExtraIndex } ~24-28 B (replaces FBuildingData ~344-368 B)

TArray<TPair<float,BuildingId>> ZIndex sorted by Z, or TMap<int32,TArray<BuildingId>> Z-bands (replaces Z-sorted CurrentBuildingData)

designs.memoryImpact: Heap per building: ~344-368 B -> ~24-28 B (12-15x reduction). 200k buildings: ~69 MB -> ~5.5 MB; 1M buildings: ~360 MB -> ~26 MB. On a host, the Records store can be dropped entirely (iterate engine arrays), leaving only Grid (~bounded, ~tens of bytes per occupied cell + 4 B per BuildingId entry) + ZIndex (~12 B/building). Derived cache (FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache/VisualBoxCache, ~152-192 B/building) eliminated outright. Redirector (leaking 4 B per lifetime-add) and quadtree (48 B/building) removed. VRAM: 256 MB -> 64 MB at 4096 (config-tunable); RTF_R8/alpha-only would cut another 4x where color isn't needed. Net at 1M buildings: roughly 616 MB (360 heap + 256 VRAM) -> ~90 MB (26 heap + 64 VRAM), ~7x.
risks: Recomputing screen position/corners every draw adds CPU per drawn building (~50-60 FLOPs/building for 4 TRS corner transforms + 2D affine + one hash lookup into ClassDrawTable). Mitigated because draw is dirty-rect-localized (only buildings in dirty cells) and the cost is dwarfed by the actual FCanvasTileItem raster; but a full redraw of a megabase recomputes everything — keep it budgeted via the existing FTickTimeBudget.

Dropping the full FTransform to Position+Yaw assumes pitch/roll/scale are never needed for the top-down draw. Verify no buildable relies on non-yaw rotation or non-uniform scale in the icon/rectangle path (cpp:762-800); splines already store world-space points so they are unaffected.

TSparseArray slot reuse changes BuildingId stability semantics vs a monotonic id — if the RCO or any future UI keys on BuildingId across a remove+add, add the generation counter to detect stale handles.

Single-precision FVector3f position at ~1 cm/px over a 750000 cm map has ~0.05 cm worst-case error at the map edge (24-bit mantissa) — visually irrelevant at 4096/8192 px, but confirm no logic compares positions for exact equality (the old operator== did FTransform.Equals at cpp:589; remove that path since identity is now the handle, not the value).

Grid cell size tuning: too-small cells inflate per-building cell-list insertions for large foundations/long belts spanning many cells; too-large cells inflate dirty-rect query cost. ~50 m is a reasonable start but should be a constant easy to tune.

Changing RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE requires editing the CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization.uasset SizeX/SizeY to match, or transforms (ORIGIN_UV/PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER, h:37-38) desync — they are constexpr off the constant so code stays self-consistent but the asset must be matched.

This is a large refactor touching the data model, both add/remove paths, the draw loop, NetSerialize (DataStructure.cpp:118-206 must serialize the slim record, not the cache), and the RCO. Ship it in the migration steps below so each is independently testable.

The 2.0-branch SceneCapture+ISM alternative would be an even bigger structural win (GPU-side rasterization, O(1) AddInstance, redraw cost independent of building count) but is a full rendering-model rewrite; this design is the data-model end-state that keeps the canvas path and is a prerequisite/complement either way (the slim store + grid feed an ISM path just as well).
implementationSketch: Step 1 (highest ROI, low risk): Introduce stable handles. Replace CurrentBuildingData (TArray) + BuildingDataIndexRedirector with a TSparseArray<FBuildingData> and store the sparse slot index as the quadtree payload. Rewrite OnBuildingDataAdd (cpp:1194) to TSparseArray::Add + quadtree.Insert(slotId, box) — delete the O(N) reindex loop (cpp:1199-1205). Rewrite OnBuildingDataRemove (cpp:1213) to quadtree.Remove(slotId, box) + Records.RemoveAt(slotId) — delete the O(N) scan (cpp:1217-1230). This alone kills the #14 ingestion spikes and the redirector leak while keeping the existing struct and quadtree.

Step 2: Extract a standalone Z-index (TArray<TPair<float,BuildingId>> or Z-bands). Move the Algo::LowerBound/UpperBound Z-range logic (cpp:663-664, OnZFilterUpdated cpp:935) onto it. Remove operator<=>(float) Z-sorting dependence (DataStructure.cpp:23-32); Records no longer need ordering. Fix the remove path's O(N) same-Z linear scan (cpp:587-605) — identity is now the handle, so the value-compare loop is deleted.

Step 3: Build ClassDrawTable (TMap<uint32,FClassDrawInfo>) once in GatherBuildables; move the per-class lookups out of FillInCache (DataStructure.cpp:264-446) into a draw-time function ComputeDrawGeometry(record, classInfo) that returns ScreenPosition/Size/Corners/Rotation. Delete the DataCache variant and VisualBoxCache fields from the record; the draw loop (cpp:714-885) calls ComputeDrawGeometry instead of reading cached fields.

Step 4: Shrink the record to FSlimBuildingRecord (ClassHash + FVector3f Position + float Yaw + Type + ExtraIndex); move spline/wire/beam extra data to side tables. Update NetSerialize (DataStructure.cpp:118-206) and the RCO (CartographRemoteCallObject.cpp) to serialize the slim record; on the host, optionally drop Records and iterate AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem per dirty cell at draw time. Fix InitialBuildableGather to take the engine map by const-ref, not by value (cpp:456).

Step 5: Swap TQuadTree for the uniform hash grid (TMap<FIntPoint,TArray<BuildingId>> or flat cell array over the fixed bounds h:28-31). Insert/erase BuildingId per overlapped cell; GetElements(dirtyRect) (cpp:686) visits overlapping cells only.

Step 6: Render fixes. Drop RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE to 4096 (config + edit CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization.uasset SizeX/SizeY). Replace the full-size ClearItem (cpp:653-660) with a clear sized to ScissorArea (MinIntX/Y..MaxIntX/Y, cpp:641-645). Replace RedrawMap's cancel-restart-on-every-event (cpp:442) with debounced DirtyCells accumulation + one budgeted redraw per quiescence window, expanding the dirty rect instead of discarding completed draw work.

Step 7 (RCO/#9): stream slices on demand from the slim store instead of materializing the whole FBufferWriter up front (CartographRemoteCallObject.cpp:48), key per-player cleanup on PlayerController logout (not just Finished/timeout), and widen the slice count from int16 to int32. Smaller slim records make this transfer 12-15x cheaper in resident memory per concurrent joiner.

designs.problem: Cartograph keeps a full second copy of the factory (CurrentBuildingData, Public/CartographGameInstanceModule.h:359) of ~344-432 B/building, a parallel never-compacted BuildingDataIndexRedirector + TQuadTree<int32> (h:365-366), a precomputed ~176 B/building screen-space DataCache (CartographDataStructure.h:60-87), and a permanently-resident 8192x8192 RGBA8 render target (h:35 = 256 MB VRAM). On every build/remove the CPU rasterizer (RedrawMapCoroutine, Private/CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:546-892) clears+redraws the canvas with a full-size ClearItem (cpp:653-660) and O(N) reindex bookkeeping (cpp:1199-1206, 1218-1230). The result is the high-memory complaint plus issue #14 (15s lag spikes, ~1h GPU TDR after placing a belt) and amplifies #9 (join crash) and #10 (no localized/budgeted redraw).
designs.designName: GPU-resident instanced map: SceneCapture2D over per-class GPU instance buffers, with engine-state-as-source-of-truth and zero CPU rasterization
designs.lens: GPU/engine-leveraging: SceneCapture2D orthographic render, per-class HISM/ISM instanced draws (one instance = one buildable, GPU-resident transform), incremental AddInstance/RemoveInstance, deferred single GPU capture, no CPU FCanvas rasterization, no parallel CPU factory copy. This is a hardening + memory-reduction of the prototype already on origin/Cartograph_2.0.
designs.approach:
Replace the data-driven CPU rasterizer with a GPU scene-graph the engine already knows how to draw fast, then "redraw" = one orthographic SceneCapture2D over that scene graph.

CORE IDEA — make the GPU instance buffer the single render-side copy. For each distinct buildable CLASS, keep ONE UInstancedStaticMeshComponent (a flat quad or a unit-box mesh, unlit material tinted by the class category color) parented to a hidden MapMarkerActor. Each live buildable becomes ONE instance: a per-instance FMatrix44f placing/scaling/rotating the quad to its world footprint, flattened to the map plane. The HISM/ISM transform buffer (FMatrix44f = 64 B/instance, GPU-resident, uploaded to a structured buffer) IS the render copy — we delete CurrentBuildingData entirely. Splines/wires/beams become thin oriented-box line instances (SPLINE_SEGMENTS instances per spline) reusing get_line_transform from the 2.0 branch.

REDRAW = GPU CAPTURE, NOT CPU LOOP. A single USceneCaptureComponent2D set to OrthoWidth = MAP_WIDTH_CENTIMETERS, projection orthographic, looking straight down, captures the whole MapMarkerActor into the existing UCanvasRenderTarget2D via CaptureSceneDeferred(). With bCaptureEveryFrame=false and CaptureSource=SCS_FinalColorLDR (or a custom unlit show-flag set), one capture rasterizes the entire factory on the GPU in a single pass whose cost is ~O(visible instances) on the rasterizer, NOT O(N) CPU DrawItem calls. A belt placement, a blueprint stamp, or a Z-filter change all collapse to: mutate instance buffers (cheap) + one CaptureSceneDeferred() next frame. The 15s game-thread stall (issue #14) disappears because the game thread no longer rasterizes; it only updates instance transforms.

INCREMENTAL MUTATION — O(1) amortized, no reindex, no leak. Keep a stable identity per buildable: a TMap<FCartographKey, FInstanceHandle> where FCartographKey is the engine's own identity (AFGBuildable* for heavy actors; {TSubclassOf, lightweight-array-index} for lightweight) and FInstanceHandle = {classComponent, instanceIndex}. The five existing hooks (LambdaAfterAddBuildable etc., cpp:115-265) call Component->AddInstance(matrix) (returns the index -> store handle) on add, and Component->RemoveInstance(index) on remove (HISM swaps the tail in and renumbers ONE moved instance; patch its handle in the map — O(1), no O(N) redirector walk, no -1 tombstone). This deletes BuildingDataIndexRedirector (h:365) and TQuadTree<int32> (h:366) and their O(N)/O(cumulative-adds) scans (cpp:1199-1206, 1218-1230) outright. GPU frustum/occlusion culling on the capture replaces the quad-tree's spatial query.

Z-FILTER WITHOUT A SORTED ARRAY. Encode each instance's world Z into a per-instance custom data float (HISM PerInstanceCustomData). The unlit material discards (clip()) fragments whose Z is outside a MinZ/MaxZ material parameter. Moving the height slider = set two scalar parameters + one re-capture, never an O(N) array re-walk (kills the OnZFilterUpdated->RedrawMap(true) full redraw, cpp:935-950, and the Z-only operator<=> coupling at CartographDataStructure.cpp:23-26). Layer toggles = per-instance custom-data layer id + material mask, same mechanism, so OnLayerConfigChanged (cpp:407-413) also becomes parameter-only.

NO SECOND CPU COPY ON THE HOST. On the host/listen-server, AFGBuildableSubsystem::GetAllBuildablesRef and AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem already hold every transform; we read them once at OnWorldLoaded to seed the instance buffers (bulk AddInstances, as 2.0 does at the world-module DispatchLifecycleEvent) and thereafter mutate incrementally via hooks. We never materialize FBuildingData per building. On dedicated-server CLIENTS we still receive data via the RCO, but deserialize directly into instance transforms + a slim TArray<FInstanceHandle> rather than full FBuildingData. The dedicated SERVER builds NO instance components and runs NO capture (it has no GPU) — it only keeps the authoritative replication snapshot, removing the server-side draw bookkeeping that amplifies #9.

WHY THIS BEATS THE SCISSOR HACK. The current branch's partial-redraw scissor (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:102-115) and the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook (cpp:322-354, taxes EVERY canvas in the game) exist only to make CPU rasterization cheaper. With SceneCapture there is no FCanvas path for the map, so the global hook is deleted (removes the system-wide per-batch tax and the cross-mod downcast hazard). The 256 MB target can also drop to 4096^2 (64 MB) since GPU MSAA/AA on the capture gives better-looking lines than 1px-per-1cm CPU lines.
designs.complexityBefore: Per build/remove event: O(N) redirector reindex (cpp:1199-1206/1218-1230) + O(N) sorted Insert/RemoveAt memmove (cpp:575/597) + O(N_localdensity) quad-tree GetElements/sort (cpp:686-708) + full or scissored CPU rasterization issuing up to ~9*N FCanvas DrawItem/co_await per full redraw. Batch of K events = O(K*N). Initial load = O(M^2) synchronous redirector pass (cpp:520-526). Full redraw / Z-filter change = O(N) CPU walk + GPU clear+repaint of 256 MB. N grows toward cumulative-lifetime-adds due to the never-compacted redirector.
designs.complexityAfter: Per build/remove event: O(1) amortized AddInstance/RemoveInstance (HISM tail-swap renumbers one instance; patch one map entry) + mark capture dirty. Redraw cost moves to the GPU as one orthographic capture, ~O(visible instances) on the rasterizer with no game-thread O(N) loop and no per-primitive co_await. Initial load = O(M) bulk AddInstances (no O(M^2) redirector). Z-filter / layer toggle = O(1) (set 2 material scalars) + one capture, replacing O(N). No quad-tree, no redirector, no sorted-array shifts, no cumulative-adds growth (RemoveInstance actually frees).
dataStructures: Per-class UHierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent (one per distinct buildable class / line-type) on a hidden MapMarkerActor; transform buffer (FMatrix44f, 64 B/instance, GPU-resident) is the ONLY render-side copy, replacing CurrentBuildingData (h:359)

TMap<FCartographKey, FInstanceHandle> for O(1) add/remove identity, where FCartographKey = engine identity (AFGBuildable* or {TSubclassOf, lightweight index}) and FInstanceHandle = {HISM*, int32 instanceIndex}; replaces BuildingDataIndexRedirector (h:365) and TQuadTree<int32> (h:366) entirely

PerInstanceCustomData floats per instance: [worldZ, layerId, categoryColorIndex] consumed by an unlit material that clip()s by MinZ/MaxZ and layer mask; replaces the Z-sorted CurrentBuildingData + OnZFilterUpdated full-redraw path

USceneCaptureComponent2D (orthographic, OrthoWidth=MAP_WIDTH_CENTIMETERS, bCaptureEveryFrame=false, CaptureSource=SCS_FinalColorLDR/unlit), capturing into the existing UCanvasRenderTarget2D (RenderTarget, h:335); GetViewOwner() override + ShowOnlyActorComponents(MapMarkerActor) to see only the marker layer

Per-class CDO-derived FBox bounding-box cache (BuildableBoundingBoxCache from the 2.0 branch's GetBuildingBoundingBox via GetCombinedClearanceBox) keyed by class, replacing the per-building precomputed FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache/VisualBoxCache (~176-216 B/building)
designs.memoryImpact: RAM: delete CurrentBuildingData (~344-432 B/building) + BuildingDataIndexRedirector (4 B/cumulative-add, leaking) + TQuadTree<int32> (~48 B/building + node overhead). Replace with one FMatrix44f (64 B) + ~12 B custom data + one TMap entry (~24 B) per LIVE building ~= ~100 B/building, GPU-resident transform offloaded from system RAM where possible. Net ~3-4x less per-building and no unbounded leak (RemoveInstance frees). At 1M buildings: from ~360-430 MB (array) + tens of MB (redirector/tree) down to ~100 MB, much of it VRAM not RAM. VRAM: render target 256 MB -> 64 MB by moving RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE to 4096 (GPU AA compensates) — net VRAM roughly flat after adding instance buffers (~64 MB at 1M instances) but the SECOND CPU copy is gone. Transient: no full-screen 256 MB clear per event (capture clears its own target once); no per-redraw 9*N DrawItem allocations.
risks: SceneCapture2D cost is per-capture, not free: a full ortho capture of a megabase each frame could itself hitch. Mitigation: bCaptureEveryFrame=false, capture only on a debounced dirty flag (coalesce many same-frame events into one capture next tick), and cap captures to <=1/frame. This is the #10 'frame-relative budget' done on the GPU side.

Render-target capture must NOT see the real world. The 2.0 branch's GetViewOwner() override + ShowOnlyActorComponents(MapMarkerActor) is the correct mechanism but is fragile across UE versions; must verify hidden/HiddenInGame flags and that the capture's show-only list resolves per-owner (the exact reason 2.0 overrode GetViewOwner).

Lightweight buildables have no stable AActor* identity; their key must be {class, array index} and that index can be reused/renumbered by the engine on its own removals. Must validate the engine's lightweight removal path (InvalidateRuntimeInstanceDataForIndex hook, cpp:206-235 already exists) keeps indices stable enough, or maintain a generation counter, else add/remove handles desync.

HISM RemoveInstance does a tail-swap that renumbers the moved instance; the map patch for that one moved instance must be atomic with the removal or handles corrupt. Lower risk than the current O(N) redirector but needs a unit test for the swap-and-patch.

Line/spline rendering as oriented box instances loses the crisp 1px CPU lines; thickness must be tuned in world units and may look different at 4096^2. GPU AA generally improves it, but belt/wire visuals need art review.

Material-based Z/layer clip() means filtered instances still cost vertex+rasterizer work (clipped in PS). For extreme megabases consider per-class component visibility toggles for whole disabled layers instead of per-instance clip, to also save vertex work.

Replacing the FCanvas pipeline removes the BlendToSimpleElementBlend translucency/rotation path; icon buildings drawn as textured quads must move to a material with the icon texture (texture array or per-class component) — more setup than the current TSoftObjectPtr draw, and icon streaming must be pinned (addresses the mid-pass AsyncLoadObject stall at cpp:758).

On dedicated-server clients the RCO transfer still exists; this design slims what it deserializes into but does not by itself fix the RCO null-deref/int16 overflow (#9) — those are separate fixes, though removing server-side draw bookkeeping reduces the concurrent load during a join.
implementationSketch: Stand up the scene graph: port UCartographGameWorldModule from origin/Cartograph_2.0 (Private/CartographGameWorldModule.cpp DispatchLifecycleEvent) into the GameFeature layout — a hidden MapMarkerActor + USceneCaptureComponent2D (orthographic, OrthoWidth=MAP_WIDTH_CENTIMETERS from h:32, looking down) capturing into the existing RenderTarget (h:335). Add the GetViewOwner() override + ShowOnlyActorComponents(MapMarkerActor) from 2.0.

Build per-class HISM components on demand (GetIsm/GetNiagaraComponentPerType pattern from 2.0) with an unlit, two-sided, translucent material; quad mesh for Normal buildings, unit-box for lines. Derive footprint from the 2.0 GetBuildingBoundingBox (GetCombinedClearanceBox + CDO fallback) cached per class — replaces FillInCache/GetBuildingSize (CartographDataStructure.cpp:264-446).

Seed at load: in OnWorldLoaded (cpp:360-396) replace the InitialBuildableGather coroutine (cpp:455-542) with a bulk pass over GetAllBuildablesRef + AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem instances calling AddInstances per class (as 2.0 does), and populate TMap<FCartographKey,FInstanceHandle>. Delete CurrentBuildingData, BuildingDataIndexRedirector, CurrentBuildingQuadTree (h:359-366) and OnBuildingDataAdd/Remove (cpp:1194-1234).

Rewire the five hooks (cpp:115-265): on add -> ComponentForClass->AddInstance(BuildToInstanceTransform(...)) and store the returned index in the key->handle map; on remove -> look up handle, RemoveInstance(index), patch the one tail-swapped instance's handle. Each hook ends by setting bCaptureDirty=true instead of RedrawMap(false).

Replace RedrawMap/RedrawMapCoroutine/ExecuteRedrawMapCoroutine (cpp:435-451, 546-892, 916+) with a debounced capture: a per-tick check that, if bCaptureDirty, calls MapCapture->CaptureSceneDeferred() once and clears the flag. Remove the full-screen ClearItem (cpp:653-660), the per-primitive co_await Budget loop, and OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled (cpp:895-913).

Move Z-filter + layer filter to the material: write worldZ/layerId/categoryColor into PerInstanceCustomData at AddInstance; OnZFilterUpdated (cpp:935-950) and OnLayerConfigChanged (cpp:407-413) now set material scalar/vector parameters (MinZ, MaxZ, layer mask) + bCaptureDirty=true. Delete the Z-only operator<=> coupling (CartographDataStructure.cpp:23-26) reliance.

Delete the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook (cpp:322-354) and the entire Util/CartographCanvasRenderItem.cpp scissor render item — no longer needed without CPU canvas rasterization. Drop RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE to 1024*4 (h:35) and the matching uasset SizeX/SizeY to halve-then-quarter VRAM; ORIGIN_UV/PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER recompute automatically.

On dedicated server (FPlatformProperties::IsServerOnly): build no MapMarkerActor/components and run no capture; keep only the authoritative replication snapshot. On dedicated-server clients, deserialize the RCO stream (CartographRemoteCallObject.cpp) directly into AddInstance calls + the handle map instead of FBuildingData.

pick.chosenDesign: Design 2: Engine-as-truth plus slim deltas (stable-handle slim record, uniform hash grid, per-class draw table, geometry recomputed on demand).
pick.rationale: All three designs find the same root cause (identity coupled to array position) and converge on the same three wins (kill the redirector, drop derived caches, shrink and scissor the target). Design 1 (minimal) is literally Design 2 Step 1; its deferred residual O(N) memmove is exactly what Design 2 sparse-array plus separate Z-index resolves. Design 3 (SceneCapture plus instanced meshes) is best for redraw cost and rightly flags the global FCanvas hook (cpp:322-354) that taxes the whole game and downcasts arbitrary render batches at cpp:342, a real cross-mod hazard. But its 2.0 prototype is verifiably unfinished (the Niagara SetAsset call at CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:109 is a no-arg stub), it loses crisp CPU lines and the icon soft-pointer path, its GetViewOwner and ShowOnlyActorComponents isolation (MapCaptureComponent2D.cpp:4) is version-fragile, and it does not fix the RCO crash (issue 9). Design 2 is the correct end-state data model regardless of renderer: a 24 to 28 byte stable-handle record plus grid plus per-class table feeds the existing canvas AND an instanced or SceneCapture path equally, making it a prerequisite to Design 3 rather than a rival. It is the biggest low-risk-per-step memory win (records 12 to 15 times smaller, derived cache gone, leak gone, host can drop the copy entirely since the engine already holds every transform at cpp:383-388), turns per-event ops toward O(1) (kills the issue-14 spikes), and stages testably. Verified against code: NetSerialize already drops scale and sends hash, location, and yaw only (DataStructure.cpp:120-143), proving Position plus Yaw is the minimal record; the corner math is duplicated (cpp:421-433 versus cpp:526-540); world bounds are compile-time constants (h:28-31) so a flat grid is trivial; lightweight removes match by value not pointer (cpp:225-232), confirming why a stable handle plus engine-as-truth is needed.
pick.mergedRecommendation:
Ship in ordered, independently-shippable phases.

PHASE 0 (days, no data-model change): (a) Scissor the clear. On the partial branch, size ClearItem to the scissor bounds already computed at cpp:641-645 instead of the full opaque ClearItem at cpp:653-660; a 67 million texel clear becomes a few hundred, directly attacking the issue-14 TDR. (b) Quarter VRAM. Set RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE to 1024 times 4 (h:35) and re-author the uasset to 4096 by 4096; ORIGIN_UV and PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER auto-recompute (h:37-38); 256 MB to 64 MB; expose as config. (c) RCO issue-9 hardening. Null-check the two unchecked InitialBuildingDataToSendPerPlayer.Find(PlayerController) derefs (RCO.cpp:73 and 87) so a logout mid-transfer no longer crashes the server; widen the int16 slice count (RCO.cpp:53,77,79,94) to int32; clean up on PlayerController logout, not just Finished or timeout.

PHASE 1 stable handles (Design 1 Step 1 equals Design 2 Step 1; highest ROI, low risk): replace CurrentBuildingData plus BuildingDataIndexRedirector with a TSparseArray of FBuildingData whose stable slot index is the quadtree payload. OnBuildingDataAdd (cpp:1194): Add plus Insert(slotId, box); DELETE the O(N) reindex (cpp:1199-1206). OnBuildingDataRemove (cpp:1213): Remove(slotId, box) plus RemoveAt(slotId); DELETE the O(N) scan (cpp:1217-1230). Delete the O(N) value-match remove scan (cpp:587-605) since identity is now the handle. Verify the UE5.3 quadtree Remove element-equality signature first. Move the Z-filter onto a separate Z-index (LowerBound and UpperBound at cpp:663-664, OnZFilterUpdated cpp:935), removing the comparator Z-sort coupling (DataStructure.cpp:23-26) so slots never shift. Result: leak gone, add and remove O(log N), initial load O(N log N).

PHASE 2 slim record plus per-class table (Design 2): build a per-class draw table once in GatherBuildables; extract ScreenPosition, Corners, Size, Rotation into a pure ComputeDrawGeometry at draw time (cpp:714 onward) and DELETE FNormalDataCache, FRectangleDataCache, VisualBoxCache (DataStructure.h:53-89), killing the duplicated corner math. Pre-resolve and pin icons before BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (cpp:630) so the loop never co-awaits AsyncLoadObject mid-canvas (cpp:758). Shrink to a slim record of class hash, single-precision position, yaw, type, and an extra-data index (about 24 to 28 bytes versus 344 to 432), with spline, wire, and beam payloads in side tables; update NetSerialize (DataStructure.cpp:118-206) and the RCO. On host, drop Records and iterate the engine arrays (cpp:383-388) per dirty cell; only dedicated-server clients keep slim Records. Swap the quadtree for a flat uniform grid over the fixed bounds (h:28-31, about 50 m cells) for O(1) add and erase. Replace RedrawMap cancel-restart (cpp:442) with debounced dirty-cell accumulation plus one budgeted redraw per quiescence window (resolves issue-10; the RedrawTimeBudget config already exists).

PHASE 3 (optional, only if megabase redraw still dominates): graft Design 3 onto the Phase-2 store. Port the 2.0 SceneCapture plus per-class instanced-mesh path (grid and table feed AddInstance and RemoveInstance), encode worldZ and layerId in per-instance custom data with a material clip, and DELETE the global FCanvas hook (cpp:322-354) and the Util CartographCanvasRenderItem scissor item. Gate on art review and GetViewOwner isolation on UE5.3.

Net at 1M buildings after Phase 2: heap about 360 MB to about 26 MB (host near 0), derived cache gone, leak gone, VRAM 256 MB to 64 MB, per-event O(1), and both issue-14 and issue-9 fixed.
pick.problem: Cartograph keeps a full second copy of the factory (CurrentBuildingData, array of FBuildingData, h:359), a never-compacted BuildingDataIndexRedirector plus a quadtree of int32 (h:365-366), per-building precomputed caches (FNormalDataCache, FRectangleDataCache, VisualBoxCache, DataStructure.h:53-89), and an 8192 by 8192 RGBA8 render target (h:35; asset verified 8192 by 8192, about 256 MB VRAM). The redirector leaks 4 bytes per lifetime placement (tombstoned to minus one at cpp:1224, never removed; documented h:361-364), forces O(N) scans on add (cpp:1199-1206) and remove (cpp:1217-1230), makes initial load O(N squared) (cpp:522-526), plus an O(N) value-match remove scan (cpp:587-605). Every redraw submits a full opaque clear (cpp:653-660) although scissor bounds are already computed (cpp:641-645). Root cause: the quadtree stores positional indices into a Z-sorted array (the comparator sorts only on Z, DataStructure.cpp:23-26), so insert and remove renumber everything and the redirector exists only to patch that up.
quickWins: Scissor the clear (cpp:653-660): size ClearItem to the scissor bounds already computed at cpp:641-645 instead of the full opaque clear; cheapest high-leverage fix for the issue-14 TDR and lag.

Quarter VRAM: RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE to 1024 times 4 (h:35) and re-author CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization.uasset to 4096 by 4096 (verified currently 8192). 256 MB to 64 MB; ORIGIN_UV and PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER auto-recompute (h:37-38); make it a config option.
Pre-resolve and pin distinct icon textures before BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (cpp:630) so the draw loop never suspends on AsyncLoadObject mid-open-canvas (cpp:758).

RCO null-deref fix (issue 9): guard the two unchecked InitialBuildingDataToSendPerPlayer.Find(PlayerController) derefs (RCO.cpp:73 and 87); a logout mid initial-data transfer crashes the dedicated server today.
RCO int16 to int32 slice count (RCO.cpp:53,77,79,94): large bases overflow the int16 slice counter on join.

Stable-ID quadtree plus delete the redirector (Design 1 Step 1): key the quadtree on a stable id; delete the O(N) reindex (cpp:1199-1206), the O(N) remove scan (cpp:1217-1230), and the O(N) value-match scan (cpp:587-605). Removes the documented hack (h:361-364) and the unbounded 4-bytes-per-placement leak; initial load O(N squared) to O(N log N).

title: Eliminate placement/dismantle lag (O(N^2) hotpaths + coroutine cancel/restart thrash + incremental data-structure mutation)

designs.problem: Placement and dismantle lag up to 15 seconds in issue 14 plus high memory caused by O of N per event ingestion an O of N squared initial load a never compacted index redirector leak and cancel restart coroutine thrash
designs.designName: Stable ID free list store plus decoupled Z index plus draw debounce
designs.lens: Minimal diff surgical fixes keeping the current architecture low risk and shippable in independent steps
designs.approach: Replace the positional index redirector with a stable building ID. Store buildings in a TSparseArray keyed by an allocation index that never moves and reuses freed slots and store that stable ID in the existing TQuadTree of int. Add and remove become O of log N with no O of N rebase and no tombstone leak. Decouple the height filter with a separate sorted Z index of Z and ID pairs and a KeyToId map for O of one removal identity which removes the need to Z sort the master array. Stop cancelling the in flight coroutine on every event and instead drain pending adds and removes immediately and cheaply into the data structures and debounce the actual draw so many events coalesce into one localized redraw. Optionally clamp the full size clear tile to the scissor rect and drop the render target from 8192 to 4096.

designs.complexityAfter: Per add and per remove O of log N an initial load of O of N log N mass dismantle of O of K log N memory of order live count with no tombstones and one coalesced localized redraw per debounce window

designs.designName: Stable-ID slab plus uniform spatial hash grid plus decoupled Z-index plus tiled persistent render target with a never-cancelled frame-budgeted compositor
designs.problem: O(N) per event and O(N squared) load on a duplicated, Z-sorted, redirector-indexed array with cancel-restart full-clear redraws. Drives 14, memory, 10, 9.
designs.lens: Best-end-state redesign of the data model and rendering for correctness and scaling to million-building factories.
designs.approach: One array conflates three roles: storage, spatial culling via the quad tree and redirector, and the Z-filter via global sort. Z-sorting renumbers positions on insert, forcing the O(N) redirector re-base, and positional ints cannot be updated cheaply in the quad tree, which is why the redirector and its tombstone leak exist. Decouple all three. STORE is a TSparseArray slab keyed by a stable BuildingId; removal is O(1) with no memmove or reindex. The record is a slim POD; drop DataCache and VisualBoxCache and recompute at draw, cutting about 344-368 bytes to about 24-40 bytes. SPATIAL is a uniform hash grid over fixed bounds with O(1) ops, replacing the quad tree and redirector. Z-INDEX is standalone. RENDER tiles the target and composites a budgeted dirty-tile set per frame, never cancelling, so a drag converges incrementally and a megabase redraw spreads over frames, fixing issue 14 and implementing issue 10. The server serializes once into a shared blob across joiners, fixing issue 9.
designs.complexityBefore: O(N) per event; O(N squared) load.
designs.complexityAfter: O(1) plus O(log N) per event; O(N) load.

risks: Recompute-at-draw needs a per-class cache; gate the global FCanvas hook on CurrentCanvas; fix the spline Reserve.
implementationSketch: Step 1, highest ROI, no rendering change: make the quad tree store stable ids so OnBuildingDataAdd at cpp 1194-1210 and OnBuildingDataRemove at cpp 1213-1234 become constant time; stop Z-sorting at cpp 520 and 573-575; build the slab in O of N at cpp 522-526; delete the redirector at h 365.
Step 2: standalone Z-index replacing the bound queries at cpp 663-664. Step 3: uniform hash grid for the TQuadTree at h 366, rewriting the localized query at cpp 686-712.

Step 4: slim record at DataStructure h 75-109, draw at cpp 714-885. Step 5: tile, per-tile clear at cpp 653-660, never Cancel at cpp 442. Step 6: gate the hook at cpp 322-354. Step 7: server snapshot at RCO cpp 42-55, widen int16 counters.

designs.problem: Placement and dismantle lag up to 15s and a one hour GPU TDR client crash in issue 14, plus full map redraw inefficiency in issue 10, join crashes in issue 9, and high memory. Root cause is a data driven CPU rasterizer that on every build or remove event mutates a Z sorted parallel array CurrentBuildingData plus a TQuadTree of int32 plus a never shrinking BuildingDataIndexRedirector with O of N scans and memmoves per element at CartographGameInstanceModule cpp 573 to 605 and 1194 to 1234, then re issues one unbounded CPU canvas pass into an 8192 by 8192 256 MB UCanvasRenderTarget2D consisting of a full screen opaque ClearItem at cpp 653 to 660 plus about nine per building tile and line draws accumulated into one FCanvas and flushed in one un yielded RHI submission at CartographCanvasRenderItem cpp 28 to 36 and 108 to 114. The co await Budget points pace only game thread emission while the GPU still receives one giant pass, the direct TDR mechanism. Every event also cancels and restarts the in flight coroutine at cpp 442 so nothing converges during a drag.
designs.designName: GPU instanced SceneCapture map: a persistent per category HISM scene graph rendered by a SceneCapture2D, with incremental O of 1 instance add and remove and coalesced single frame captures
designs.lens: GPU and engine leveraging via SceneCapture2D plus instanced static meshes HISM and ISM plus per category batching plus GPU bounded captures. Move rasterization off the game thread and off the CPU entirely, make redraw a fixed cost GPU operation independent of building count, and let the engine transform cull and batch pipeline do the work the mod currently does by hand on the CPU.
designs.approach: Replace the entire CPU canvas rasterizer with a GPU scene capture pipeline the engine already optimizes, and replace the bespoke spatial bookkeeping with the instancing system own per instance management. This is the structural inversion proven viable on origin Cartograph_2.0 at CartographGameWorldModule cpp 31 to 95, hardened here for incrementality and TDR safety. The core model is a top down orthographic camera over a flat marker scene. First, a hidden AMapMarkerActor owns one UHierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent or HISM per buildable category, batching by draw category rather than raw class to keep component count in the hundreds, which is exactly the 2.0 per type idea. Each buildable becomes ONE instance, a unit quad or box mesh whose per instance FTransform encodes world XY position, planar rotation, and XY scale equal to the building footprint from the same GetBuildingSize and GetCombinedClearanceBox source the CPU path uses at DataStructure cpp 373 and 585. Color and icon per class is a material parameter on that component MID rather than per building CPU state. Splines, belts, pipes, wires and beams become thin oriented box instances via the 2.0 get_line_transform helper, so a belt is O of segments instances rather than O of segments CPU line draws per redraw. Second, a single UMapCaptureComponent2D that is Orthographic with OrthoWidth MAP_WIDTH_CENTIMETERS, above the world looking straight down, with ShowOnlyComponents equal to the marker HISMs using the 2.0 GetViewOwner override as the minimal correct mechanism, and bCaptureEveryFrame false. A redraw is exactly one CaptureSceneDeferred into the existing RenderTarget. The GPU instanced pipeline transforms, frustum and occlusion culls and batches ALL instances in hardware in one pass whose cost scales with visible on screen instances and not total or changed count, and it is internally chunked by HISM cluster culling, so it cannot become one monolithic un yielded batched draw the way the FCanvas path does at CartographCanvasRenderItem cpp 28. This removes the issue 14 TDR mechanism at the root. Third are incremental updates, the part 2.0 never solved. Keep a tiny stable handle store, a TMap from EventKey to FInstanceRef holding a HISM pointer and an int32 InstanceIndex, where EventKey is the engine own identity for the buildable, an AFGBuildable pointer for heavy buildables or a class plus lightweight index pair for lightweight ones, the exact keys the hooks already receive at cpp 177 to 235. On the three add hooks compute one FTransform, call HISM AddInstance which is O of 1 amortized, and store the returned index. On the two remove hooks look up FInstanceRef, call HISM RemoveInstance, and patch the one swapped neighbor index since HISM remove swaps last into hole, which is O of 1 and not O of N. This deletes CurrentBuildingData, BuildingDataIndexRedirector, the TQuadTree int32, the LowerBound plus linear scan remove at cpp 584 to 605, and the O of N redirector reindex loops at cpp 1199 to 1205 and 1218 to 1230, which is every per event O of N cost in the digest. No tombstones, no parallel array, no second full copy. Fourth are coalescing and no cancel restart. Hooks no longer call RedrawMap false, they only mutate instances and set a bDirtyCapture flag, and a per frame or debounced tick issues at most one CaptureSceneDeferred if dirty. Instances added mid drag are already in the scene so each capture reflects current truth, nothing to throw away and no coroutine to cancel, which kills the cancel restart thrash. This is exactly the issue 10 coalesced redraw with a frame relative budget, and the explicit full redraw button issue 10 asks for is just an on demand capture. Fifth is Z filter and layers without a sorted array. The height filter is MinZ and MaxZ material scalar params and the instance world Z already in its transform is clipped in the shader by discard outside range, so a Z slider change is a param set plus one capture which is O of 1 rather than OnZFilterUpdated to RedrawMap true doing an O of N array re walk plus full RT clear at cpp 935 and 676 to 682. Layer toggle is SetVisibility false on the affected per category HISM plus one capture. Sixth is memory. Make RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE a config option defaulting to 4096, a header one liner plus matching uasset SizeX and SizeY, cutting the fixed 256 MB to 64 MB and quartering every capture fill bandwidth, and tiled capture by re aiming the ortho per dirty tile into RT subregions can go lower. Per building CPU footprint collapses from about 344 to 432 bytes FBuildingData to one about 64 byte HISM FInstanceTransform plus a about 16 byte map entry, an 8 to 15 times reduction, and the unbounded redirector and quadtree growth behind the one hour issue 14 timeline is gone. The dedicated server keeps a slim authoritative list for RCO replication only and never builds HISMs.

title: Bound GPU/render cost to avoid TDR client crash and converge smoothly (rendering structure, tiling/LOD, frame-relative budget per #10)

designs.problem: Cartograph redraws the entire factory into a single 8192x8192 (256 MB RGBA8) UCanvasRenderTarget2D via one open FCanvas pass per build/remove event. The per-tick FTickTimeBudget (RedrawMapCoroutine, CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:557) bounds only game-thread element EMISSION; every emitted FCanvasTileItem/draw_line is accumulated into one FCanvas (opened at :630, flushed in OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled :901) and submitted as ONE GPU flush via FCartographCanvasRenderItem::Render_GameThread (CartographCanvasRenderItem.cpp:89-121). A full redraw of a megabase emits ~5-9 primitives/building (rectangle=1 tile+4 lines :800-812; spline=8 lines :826-831) so 100k+ buildings => ~0.5-1M batched primitives rasterized into the 8192^2 target in a SINGLE present interval, exceeding the Windows TDR threshold (~2s) -> GPU device reset -> client crash (#14, 'GPU driver timeout after placing a belt'). Two amplifiers feed the same single pass: (a) a full-size opaque ClearItem covering {0,0}..{8192,8192} is emitted on EVERY redraw (:653-660), adding a 67M-texel fill, and (b) build promotion to bRedrawEntirely (OnZFilterUpdated->RedrawMap(true) :948, init :541) turns a 1-belt placement into a whole-factory re-emit. The RedrawTimeBudget config is a false safety: it can stretch a redraw across many frames yet still produce one giant GPU submission.
designs.designName: Multi-frame GPU flush chunking + scissored clear + persistent target (bound the single pass without changing the pipeline)
designs.lens: Minimal-diff, surgical fixes that keep the current architecture (sorted CurrentBuildingData + TQuadTree + scissor-clip + UE5Coro coroutine) but remove the worst GPU/complexity hazards. Optimize for low risk and shippability.
designs.approach:
The root cause is that co_await Budget paces CPU emission but never flushes to the GPU, so the entire factory lands in one RHI submission. The minimal-diff fix is to make the GPU cost per frame bounded by the SAME mechanism that already bounds CPU cost: end and re-begin the canvas periodically inside the draw loop so each frame submits only a chunk.

(1) CHUNKED GPU FLUSH (the TDR fix, ~30 lines). Today BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (:630) opens one FCanvas for the whole redraw and EndDraw runs once in OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled (:901). Change the draw loop (:714-885) so that after a bounded number of EMITTED PRIMITIVES per frame (a new PrimitivesThisPass counter, threshold from a new config field MaxPrimitivesPerFrame, e.g. 20000), we EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget(RenderContext), co_await NextTick(), then BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget again, WITHOUT re-issuing the clear and WITHOUT resetting ScissorArea. Because the render target is persistent (a UCanvasRenderTarget2D is not auto-cleared between BeginDraw cycles - we already rely on this for partial redraws), the previously drawn chunk stays resident and the next chunk composites on top. This converts the single O(primitives) GPU submission into ceil(primitives / MaxPrimitivesPerFrame) submissions, each capped to ~20k primitives -> each present interval does bounded GPU work -> no TDR. The existing co_await Budget yields stay as-is for CPU; the new flush boundary is what bounds the GPU. This is the SAME multi-frame strategy origin/Cartograph_2.0 achieves via SceneCapture, but achieved by re-entering the existing canvas rather than re-architecting to instanced rendering.

(2) SCISSORED CLEAR (removes the per-redraw 256 MB fill, ~10 lines). The ClearItem at :653-660 is always full-size and pushed through the batched-elements pixel pipeline. Replace it: on partial redraws size the ClearItem to the already-computed scissor bounds {MinIntX,MinIntY}..{MaxIntX,MaxIntY} (computed at :641-645) instead of {0,0}..{8192,8192}; on entire redraws prefer a hardware clear via UKismetRenderingLibrary::ClearRenderTarget2D before BeginDraw rather than a rasterized opaque quad. This eliminates the 67M-texel opaque overwrite on every event and means each chunk-flush (from change 1) only clears its own dirty region (full redraws clear once up front, not per chunk).

(3) STABLE-HANDLE REDIRECTOR (kills O(N) per-event + the tombstone leak, the lag-spike + memory fix, ~40 lines). The redirector (h:365) stores absolute CurrentBuildingData indices, so OnBuildingDataAdd (:1199-1205) and OnBuildingDataRemove (:1218-1230) each do an O(N) full-array shift on every single building, and the array never shrinks (-1 tombstones leak forever). Minimal surgical replacement that keeps TQuadTree<int32>: store a STABLE handle (monotonic uint32 NextHandle) as the quadtree element value instead of an array position, and keep two maps: TMap<uint32,int32> HandleToIndex and a parallel TArray<uint32> IndexToHandle aligned with CurrentBuildingData. On add: assign handle = NextHandle++, Insert(handle, box), set HandleToIndex[handle]=Pos, and because CurrentBuildingData.Insert shifts indices we still must fix up HandleToIndex - BUT we can avoid the O(N) shift entirely by NOT keeping CurrentBuildingData index in the map and instead storing the handle directly; resolve quadtree results (GetElements at :686) handle->index via HandleToIndex. On remove: QuadTree.Remove(handle, box) is O(log N) and HandleToIndex.Remove(handle) is O(1) - no scan, no tombstone. The remaining O(N) is CurrentBuildingData.Insert/RemoveAt itself (sorted-by-Z array shift); to keep this surgical and low-risk, KEEP the sorted array but fix HandleToIndex incrementally: after Insert at Pos, the shift only affects entries with index>=Pos, which is still O(N) in the map. To make the WHOLE add/remove O(log N) we instead store the handle (not the index) in the quadtree AND in a side TMap<uint32,FBuildingData*-equivalent>; the simplest correct minimal form is to stop sorting CurrentBuildingData and keep it as a TSparseArray<FBuildingData> (stable slots = the handle), with a SEPARATE lazily-sorted Z-index built only when a full/Z-filtered redraw needs ordering. This removes both O(N) scans and the leak while touching only OnBuildingDataAdd/Remove, the two GetElements call sites, and the Z-range selection at :663-664.

INITIAL-LOAD QUICK WIN (1 line, zero risk, independent): InitialBuildableGather (:520-526) sorts then calls OnBuildingDataAdd(i) for every i, and because the redirector only holds values <Pos during a monotonically increasing build, the O(N) increment branch at :1201 is PROVABLY never taken - the inner loop is pure wasted work, O(N^2) for nothing. Even without change (3), guarding InitialBuildableGather to bulk-build the redirector/handle map in one O(N) pass (skip the per-element OnBuildingDataAdd scan during initial load) eliminates the multi-second-to-minute load hang (#1/#3) for free.

Phasing for shippability: ship (1)+(2) first - they alone resolve the TDR crash (#14) and a large memory write-bandwidth cost with ~50 lines and no data-structure change, lowest risk. Ship the InitialBuildableGather one-line guard alongside. Ship (3) second as it changes a data structure (higher review surface) but is independently testable.
designs.complexityBefore: Per build/remove event: O(N) redirector scan (add :1199 / remove :1218) + O(N) CurrentBuildingData.Insert/RemoveAt shift + (on remove) O(M) same-Z linear match (:587-605), where N=total buildings ever added since last full gather (redirector never shrinks). Initial load: O(N^2) (InitialBuildableGather :522-526, fully synchronous, uninterruptible). GPU: ONE unbounded RHI submission of O(primitives)=O(5-9*N) rasterized into 8192^2 per redraw, plus a full 67M-texel opaque clear per redraw. TDR when single-pass GPU time > ~2s.
designs.complexityAfter: Per build/remove event: O(log N) quadtree insert/remove + O(1) handle-map op; CurrentBuildingData becomes TSparseArray with O(1) slot add/free (no shift, no tombstone leak); Z-ordering moved to a lazily-rebuilt side index. Initial load: O(N log N) (one bulk handle-map pass + one sort), interruptible. GPU: ceil(primitives / MaxPrimitivesPerFrame) bounded submissions, each <= ~20k primitives per present interval (no single pass can exceed the budget -> no TDR); clear restricted to the dirty scissor rect (partial) or one hardware clear (full), eliminating the per-event 67M-texel fill.
dataStructures: TMap<uint32,int32> HandleToIndex (or TSparseArray<FBuildingData> with slot==handle) replacing TArray<int32> BuildingDataIndexRedirector (h:365)
uint32 NextHandle monotonic counter
Keep TQuadTree<int32> (h:366) but its int32 payload becomes a stable handle, not an array index
Lazily-rebuilt TArray<TPair<float,uint32>> or sorted index for the Z-filter range query (replaces relying on CurrentBuildingData being globally Z-sorted at :663-664)
New config fields in FCartograph_ConfigStruct (Cartograph_ConfigStruct.h:13-16): MaxPrimitivesPerFrame, plus reuse RedrawTimeBudget
int32 PrimitivesThisPass local counter in RedrawMapCoroutine
designs.memoryImpact: Removes the unbounded redirector leak: today BuildingDataIndexRedirector grows by 4 B per lifetime ADD and never frees (-1 tombstones), so a long churn session (the #14 belt-spam repro) leaks ~4 B * cumulative-adds monotonically. After: HandleToIndex holds one entry per LIVE building, freed O(1) on remove (~12-16 B/entry but bounded by live count, net win after any churn). No change to the dominant 256 MB render-target VRAM (that needs the orthogonal asset resize to 4096 -> 64 MB, called out as a separate one-asset lever, not in this diff to keep risk low). Chunked flush adds zero resident memory (reuses the same RenderContext). Net: eliminates the only monotonic memory leak in the hot path; render-target VRAM unchanged by this PR.
risks: Re-entering BeginDraw/EndDraw mid-redraw: the existing comment at :624-626 notes lines went 'crazy' when EndDraw/BeginDraw happened in the same frame without a NextTick delay - the chunk boundary MUST co_await NextTick() between EndDraw and the next BeginDraw (which we do), but verify the persistent target is not implicitly cleared by the second BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget on any RHI backend; if it is, the chunk approach needs the target marked to preserve contents.

ScissorArea is read on the render thread (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:104) and written on the game thread (:635/645); chunked flushing keeps ScissorArea constant for a whole redraw so this stays safe, but DO NOT mutate ScissorArea between chunks.

Cancellation interaction: RedrawMap cancels the in-flight coroutine on every event (:442) and OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled flushes whatever is open (:901). With chunked flush, a cancel mid-redraw leaves a partially-composited map (some chunks drawn, some not) until the restart completes - acceptable for a minimap but the restart must redraw the SAME region; the existing cancel-restart-from-scratch already re-emits, so partial state self-heals on the next completion. Confirm the persistent target isn't left with a half-cleared band.

Dropping the global Z-sort (change 3) changes the order buildings are drawn; draw order currently follows Z (overlap resolution). If two buildings overlap in screen space, the higher-Z one must draw last - the lazily-rebuilt Z-index must preserve this for the bRedrawEntirely path (:679). Low impact for a top-down minimap but verify icons/foundations layer correctly.

TSparseArray change touches the RCO transfer (RCO.cpp serializes CurrentBuildingData) and ClientUpdateBuildingData - keep the wire format iterating live elements only; a sparse array with holes must serialize compacted. This widens the diff for change (3), which is why it ships SECOND, after the TDR fix.

MaxPrimitivesPerFrame tuned too low makes a full redraw take many seconds of wall-clock (many frames); too high re-risks TDR. Needs a conservative default (~20k) and exposure as config like the existing time budgets.
implementationSketch: Add MaxPrimitivesPerFrame to FCartograph_ConfigStruct (Cartograph_ConfigStruct.h, next to RedrawTimeBudget:16); read it in RedrawMapCoroutine alongside the existing Budget (:556-557).

In RedrawMapCoroutine draw loop (:714-885), add an int32 PrimitivesThisPass; increment it per DrawItem/draw_line. When it crosses MaxPrimitivesPerFrame: UKismetRenderingLibrary::EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget(this, RenderContext); co_await UE5Coro::Latent::NextTick(); BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget(...) re-opening the SAME RenderTarget; refresh CurrentCanvas; reset PrimitivesThisPass=0. Do NOT re-emit ClearItem and do NOT touch ScissorArea on re-entry.

Replace the full-size ClearItem (:653-660): for the partial path build the tile at position {MinIntX,MinIntY} with size {MaxIntX-MinIntX, MaxIntY-MinIntY} (from :641-645); for the entire path call UKismetRenderingLibrary::ClearRenderTarget2D(this, RenderTarget, {0,0,0,0}) once before the draw loop instead of the opaque quad.

Guard InitialBuildableGather (:522-526): replace the per-element OnBuildingDataAdd loop with a single bulk pass that builds the quadtree + handle map without the O(N) reindex branch (the branch is never taken during monotonic load). This is independently shippable and removes the load hang.

(Phase 2) Replace TArray<int32> BuildingDataIndexRedirector with TMap<uint32,int32> HandleToIndex + uint32 NextHandle; quadtree stores handles. Rewrite OnBuildingDataAdd (:1194-1210) to Insert(handle,box)+map.Add and OnBuildingDataRemove (:1213-1234) to QuadTree.Remove(handle,box)+map.Remove(handle) - both O(log N)/O(1), no scan, no tombstone. Update the two GetElements resolution sites (:689-692) to map handle->index.

(Phase 2) Convert CurrentBuildingData to TSparseArray<FBuildingData> so slots are stable (handle==slot) and add/remove avoid the O(N) Insert/RemoveAt shift; build a lazily-rebuilt Z-sorted index for the :663-664 range selection and the bRedrawEntirely ordered walk (:679); update RCO serialization to iterate live elements compacted.

Validate on a large save: place/remove a belt repeatedly for >5 min (the #14 repro), confirm no TDR, flat per-event CPU (no upward drift), and stable memory; confirm partial redraws still clip correctly via the unchanged ScissorArea path.

designs.problem: Cartograph re-renders the entire factory into one 8192x8192 (256 MB) UCanvasRenderTarget2D every build/remove event via a CPU canvas pipeline. The whole redraw is accumulated into ONE FCanvas and flushed in a single GPU pass in OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled (cpp:901 EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget), so co_await Budget (cpp:577/607/801/830/884) only paces the game thread that EMITS batched elements; it never bounds the GPU. A full redraw of a megabase emits ~0.5-1M primitives drawn in one FBatchedElements::Draw submission (CartographCanvasRenderItem.cpp:108) into a 67M-texel target -> exceeds the Windows TDR threshold (~2s) -> driver reset -> client crash (#14).
