Goal under the best-end-state lens: bound GPU cost per frame to a fixed budget so a single submission can never TDR, and converge smoothly even on a 1M-building base, while implementing #10's localized-redraw + frame-budget + explicit-full-redraw asks.
designs.designName: Persistent tiled render target with per-tile dirty tracking and a frame-relative GPU draw-call budget (multi-frame incremental compositing)
designs.lens: Best-end-state redesign of the data model and rendering, optimized for correctness and scaling to million-building factories even if the change is larger.
designs.approach:
Replace the monolithic single-canvas-single-flush model with a PERSISTENT tiled render target that is composited incrementally across frames under a hard per-frame GPU budget. Three coupled changes:

1) TILE THE TARGET. Partition the 8192x8192 surface (or 4096 after the orthogonal VRAM reduction) into a fixed grid of T x T pixel tiles (T=512 -> 16x16=256 tiles at 8192; T=512 -> 8x8=64 tiles at 4096). A tile is the unit of clear+redraw. The render target itself stays a single texture (so the UI samples one texture, no atlas seams), but all clear/draw work is SCISSORED to one tile at a time. This is the decisive property: the GPU cost of clearing+redrawing ONE tile is bounded by tile area (512x512=262k texels) times the building density inside that tile's world AABB, never by total factory size. A tile can therefore never TDR.

2) PER-TILE DIRTY SET + FRAME BUDGET. Maintain TBitArray (or TSet<FIntPoint>) DirtyTiles over the tile grid. On each build/remove event, compute the changed building's screen AABB (already available as VisualBoxCache mapped through world_position_to_screen_position) and mark every overlapping tile dirty. The redraw coroutine becomes a steady-state pump: each game-thread tick it pops up to K dirty tiles (K driven by a config DrawCallsPerFrame / TileBudgetPerFrame), and for EACH popped tile does an INDEPENDENT BeginDraw/EndDraw cycle: set scissor to that tile, clear that tile (FCanvasTileItem sized to the tile, not the full surface), query the spatial index for buildings overlapping the tile's world AABB, draw them, then EndDraw -> this flushes a bounded GPU submission and yields. Because EndDraw happens per tile (or per small batch of tiles), GPU work per submission is bounded by K x (tile cost), and the budget is enforced at flush granularity, not emit granularity. This is what actually fixes #14: the GPU can no longer be handed an unbounded pass.

3) NO CANCEL/RESTART; DIRTY STATE IS THE QUEUE. Build/remove hooks (cpp:142/173/202/234/264) and the multicast path (CartographModSubsystem.cpp:46) stop calling RedrawMap(false)->Cancel(). Instead they (a) apply the cheap incremental data-structure mutation immediately and (b) OR the changed AABB's tiles into DirtyTiles. The compositing pump runs continuously while DirtyTiles is non-empty. Completed tile work is NEVER thrown away; new events only ADD dirty tiles. A "full redraw" (init, OnZFilterUpdated cpp:948, OnLayerConfigChanged cpp:413) simply marks ALL tiles dirty and lets the pump drain them over many frames at the same fixed per-frame cost -> a 1M-building full redraw is spread over seconds of bounded frames instead of one TDR-inducing pass. The explicit user-triggered full-redraw button #10 asks for is then trivially "DirtyTiles.SetRange(All)".

To make per-tile queries O(overlap) instead of O(N), the data model is decoupled from array position: a stable-id store (TSparseArray<FSlimBuildingRecord> with generation handles) feeds a uniform spatial hash grid TMap<FIntPoint,TArray<BuildingId>> sized to ~tile granularity, replacing TQuadTree<int32> + BuildingDataIndexRedirector entirely (kills the O(N)/O(cumulative-adds) scans at cpp:1199-1205/1218-1230 and the tombstone leak). The Z-filter moves to a separate sorted Z-index (sorted TArray<TPair<float,BuildingId>>), so storage no longer needs Z-ordering. Draw-time caches (ScreenPosition, Corners, Size, Rotation) are recomputed per building when its tile is drawn (FillInCache logic moved into the draw loop, keyed by classHash into per-CLASS lookups), eliminating the ~150-176 B/building DataCache and the duplicate VisualBoxCache. The tile pump becomes the single place GPU cost is metered.

Optional LOD layer (scaling tier): pre-render coarse zoom levels into mip-like lower-res tile sets so the UI does not need the full 8192 base resident when zoomed out; only the currently-viewed zoom's tile band needs to be hot. This is the path to dropping the fixed VRAM floor further, but it is independent of the TDR fix and can ship later.
designs.complexityBefore: Per build/remove event: O(N) redirector scan (cpp:1199-1205/1218-1230, N=cumulative lifetime adds) + O(N) array memmove (cpp:575/597) + O(N) same-Z linear match on remove (cpp:587-605). Per redraw GPU: ONE unbounded submission of O(drawn primitives) = O(~5N-9N) for a full redraw, with no per-frame cap (TDR). Full clear: O(8192^2)=67M texels bandwidth per redraw regardless of dirty area. Convergence under a drag of E events: zero completed frames (cancel/restart) until idle, then one O(N) pass.
designs.complexityAfter: Per build/remove event: O(1) sparse-array slot + O(1) grid cell insert/erase + O(log N) Z-index update + O(tilesOverlapped) dirty-mark (small constant). Per frame GPU: bounded by config K tiles x tile-area, a FIXED cap independent of N -> cannot TDR by construction. Full redraw: same fixed per-frame cost, amortized over ceil(TotalDirtyTiles/K) frames = O(tiles) frames, each bounded. Clear bandwidth: O(K x tileArea) per frame instead of O(8192^2). Convergence under a drag of E events: pump keeps producing completed tiles every frame; dirty set bounded by touched tiles, work never discarded.
dataStructures: TSparseArray<FSlimBuildingRecord> with generation handles as the stable-id master store (replaces TArray<FBuildingData> CurrentBuildingData at h:359); FSlimBuildingRecord = {uint32 classHash, FTransform transform, slim spline/wire/beam extra} with draw caches recomputed on demand

Uniform spatial hash grid TMap<FIntPoint,TArray<BuildingId>> over fixed world bounds (replaces TQuadTree<int32> at h:366 and deletes BuildingDataIndexRedirector at h:365), cell size ~= tile world footprint for O(1) insert/remove and O(overlap) tile queries
Sorted Z-index TArray<TPair<float,BuildingId>> for the height filter (replaces the Z-sorted ordering of CurrentBuildingData; decouples Z-filter from storage)
TBitArray DirtyTiles over the tile grid (the persistent redraw queue; replaces the single FBox2D RedrawArea at h:374 and the cancel/restart IsPendingRedraw flags)
Tile descriptor table: per-tile world AABB + screen scissor rect precomputed once (the tiling of RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE)

Persistent single UCanvasRenderTarget2D (kept at h:335) but never fully cleared after init; per-CLASS draw-data cache keyed by classHash (CategoryData/SplineData/WireData/Size/Rotation) replacing per-building DataCache
designs.memoryImpact: Removes per-building DataCache (~150-176 B) + duplicate VisualBoxCache (~40 B) by recomputing at draw time -> shrinks the master record from ~344-368 B to ~24-40 B (8-15x), ~72 MB->~6 MB at 200k, ~360 MB->~30 MB at 1M. Deletes BuildingDataIndexRedirector (4 B/cumulative-add, leaking) and the 48 B/building TQuadTree FBox2D payload, replacing with a grid (~8-16 B/building amortized) and a Z-index (~12 B/building). DirtyTiles is negligible (256 bits at 8192/T=512). Render target VRAM is unchanged by this design (256 MB at 8192) UNTIL the orthogonal one-line drop to RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE=1024*4 -> 64 MB; LOD tile sets add ~33% if enabled. Net resident memory for a 1M-building base drops from ~600+ MB (array+caches+redirector+quadtree+256 MB RT) to roughly ~100-130 MB (slim store + grid + Z-index + 64 MB RT), addressing the high-memory complaint and #14's ~1h growth-to-TDR.
risks: Per-tile BeginDraw/EndDraw cycles have fixed CPU/RHI overhead; too many small tiles per frame (K too high) trades TDR for game-thread stutter. Mitigate with a config TileBudget and tile size tuned so one tile is a meaningful unit of work (512px is a reasonable start); profile to set K.

BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget per tile may re-clear or reset state the author does not expect; the existing comment at cpp:624-626 about lines going crazy when BeginDraw/EndDraw share a frame suggests render-target state timing is fragile. Need a co_await NextTick discipline between flushes (already the existing pattern) and to verify scissored clear does not bleed into neighbor tiles.

Recomputing draw caches at draw time re-runs per-CLASS TMap lookups (GetBuildingSize/BuildableSizeOverrideMap/category lookups). Must cache these PER CLASS keyed by classHash (a few hundred entries) so recompute is FLOPs + 1 hash lookup, not N lookups; otherwise draw-time CPU regresses.

Splines/belts span many tiles; a long belt marks a row of tiles dirty and is redrawn (clipped) in each. Acceptable since clipped cost is bounded, but a belt touching K tiles costs K partial draws. Tune tile size against typical belt length, or special-case long splines into a dedicated low-frequency layer.

Async icon loading mid-pass (cpp:755-758) must move OUT of the per-tile flush: pre-resolve/pin all icon textures before compositing so a tile flush never suspends on I/O and never produces a partial tile. Pin only while the feature is active.

Stable-id store + grid + Z-index is a large rewrite of InitialBuildableGather, RedrawMapCoroutine, OnBuildingDataAdd/Remove, and the NetSerialize/RCO path (FBuildingData is the wire type). Sequence it: ship the data-model swap first (kills #14 CPU spikes + leak), then layer tiling on top.

Multiplayer: dirty-tile pump is client-side render; the server must still replicate deltas. The existing reliable per-event multicast (CartographModSubsystem.cpp) should be coalesced so the client's dirty set is fed by batched deltas, not per-event reliable RPCs (separate fix, but interacts with convergence).
implementationSketch: Phase 0 (orthogonal, 1 line + 1 asset): set RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE = 1024*4 (CartographGameInstanceModule.h:35) and match SizeX/SizeY in Content/UI/CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization.uasset to 4096; ORIGIN_UV/PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER are constexpr off it so transforms stay self-consistent. Cuts VRAM 256->64 MB and every clear/draw bandwidth 4x immediately.

Phase 1 data-model swap (highest ROI for #14 CPU/leak): replace CurrentBuildingData TArray + BuildingDataIndexRedirector + TQuadTree<int32> (h:359/365/366) with TSparseArray<FSlimBuildingRecord> + TMap<FIntPoint,TArray<BuildingId>> grid + sorted Z-index. Rewrite OnBuildingDataAdd/OnBuildingDataRemove (cpp:1194-1234) to O(1) grid insert/erase + O(log N) Z-index, deleting the redirector scans. Rewrite InitialBuildableGather (cpp:455-542) to bulk-fill the store/grid/Z-index in O(N log N) (single Z-index sort) instead of the O(N^2) per-element OnBuildingDataAdd loop at cpp:522-526. Move FillInCache geometry (CartographDataStructure.cpp FillInCache/FillInVisualBoxCache) into a per-CLASS cache + a draw-time recompute helper.

Phase 2 tiling: add a tile grid descriptor (tileSize, world AABB + scissor per tile) and TBitArray DirtyTiles. Add a function MarkTilesDirty(FBox2D screenAABB). Point all build/remove hooks (cpp:142/173/202/234/264) and the multicast handler at the incremental data mutation + MarkTilesDirty instead of RedrawMap(false). Replace OnZFilterUpdated->RedrawMap(true) (cpp:948) and OnLayerConfigChanged (cpp:413) with DirtyTiles.SetRange(all). Add an explicit 'Full Redraw' UI command (reuse the SetOpenMap/EnhancedInput gating pattern from origin/show_buildable_ui) that also sets all tiles dirty.

Phase 3 the pump: rewrite RedrawMapCoroutine (cpp:546-892) into a steady-state loop: while DirtyTiles non-empty, pop up to K=TileBudgetPerFrame tiles; for each tile do BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget, set ScissorArea to the tile rect (reuse the std::array<uint32,4> ScissorArea + FCartographCanvasRenderItem scissor path at CanvasRenderItem.cpp:104-105 unchanged), draw an FCanvasTileItem clear SIZED TO THE TILE (not RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE, fixing cpp:653-660), query the grid for buildings overlapping the tile world AABB intersected with the Z-index range, draw them (recomputing caches), then EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget to flush a bounded submission; co_await NextTick between flush batches. Remove the Cancel() in RedrawMap (cpp:442) and the IsPendingRedraw cancel/restart in OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled (cpp:905-912); the pump is the only redraw driver. Replace the per-primitive co_await Budget (cpp:801/806-811/830) with one yield per tile (or per small building batch).

Phase 4 hygiene: pre-resolve/pin all icon textures before the pump so the draw loop never co_awaits AsyncLoadObject (cpp:755-758) mid-flush. Add config knobs TileSize and TileBudgetPerFrame alongside the existing RedrawTimeBudget. Update the FBuildingData wire type / RCO serialization to the slim record (CartographDataStructure NetSerialize + CartographRemoteCallObject) since DataCache/VisualBoxCache are no longer stored.

Validation: with a 1M-building save, confirm (a) no single GPU submission exceeds the budget (RenderDoc/GPU profiler), (b) placing/removing a belt marks only the overlapping tiles dirty and produces no frame spike (#14), (c) a full redraw drains over many bounded frames without TDR (#10), (d) resident memory drops per the deltas above, (e) Z-filter and layer toggles re-composite only via dirty tiles.

designs.designName: GPU map atlas compositor with tiled dirty queue and per-frame GPU budget
designs.problem: Cartograph renders the entire factory into one 8192x8192 RGBA8 render target (RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE=1024*8, h:35) via the CPU coroutine RedrawMapCoroutine (cpp:546-892). Every build/remove calls RedrawMap(false) (cpp:142,173,202); Z-filter/layer toggles call RedrawMap(true) (cpp:948,411). Each redraw issues a full-screen opaque ClearItem (cpp:653-660), then per building emits 1 tile + 4 lines (rects cpp:791-812) or up to 8 lines (splines cpp:826-831), all flushed in ONE render-thread pass (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:89). The Budget yields bound only the game thread, never the GPU. So 256 MB VRAM is resident at load (cleared cpp:394); a full redraw is an unbounded single GPU submission of ~9N primitives that exceeds the Windows TDR threshold and resets the driver (#14 crash after a belt); and RedrawMap cancels the in-flight coroutine on every event (cpp:442) so the map never converges under a build-drag (#14 15s spikes; #10 inefficiency). Scissor (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:104-105) clips raster but the clear tile and monolithic flush remain; full redraws bypass culling (cpp:676-682).
designs.lens: GPU/engine-leveraging: persistent partially-updated atlas (never fully cleared), instanced ISM/Niagara draws plus an orthographic SceneCapture2D, a tiled dirty-rect queue with an RHI scissor, and a hard per-frame GPU budget. Use the engine's AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem and the Cartograph_2.0 instanced path instead of CPU FCanvasTileItem rasterization plus a parallel CPU copy of the factory.
designs.approach: Three independently-shippable inversions that move cost from O(N) CPU draw of the whole factory in one GPU submission, repeatedly, to O(dirty area) GPU draw bounded per frame into a persistent target. ONE, persistent atlas plus per-tile dirty queue: replace the monolithic target with a logical tile grid (e.g. 32x32 of 256px over the 8192 space, keeping world_position_to_screen_position h:431) and a TSet of FIntPoint DirtyTiles; on add/remove mark only tiles overlapping the building VisualBoxCache, replacing the single-AABB RedrawArea accumulation (cpp:570,593) whose union balloons across far-apart edits (the #10 over-draw); per frame pop budgeted dirty tiles, do a TRUE scissored RHIClear (ClearRenderTargetView under SetScissorRect, reusing ScissorArea at CanvasRenderItem.cpp:104-105), then draw only buildings overlapping that tile. The full-screen opaque clear quad becomes a free hardware RTV clear of a few tiles; a single-belt edit touches 1-4 tiles, not 8192x8192. TWO, hard per-frame GPU budget: the TDR cause is the whole accumulated FCanvas flushing in ONE pass (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:89); change the coroutine to EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (cpp:901) after B primitives/tiles, co_await NextTick, re-Begin (cpp:630) next frame, capping every submission (e.g. 20k prims) so the 2s TDR is structurally impossible; the persistent atlas makes a half-finished frame a consistent partial atlas, not a torn clear; one unbounded pass becomes K bounded passes across K frames (resolves #14 belt TDR, gives #10 a real frame-relative budget instead of the game-thread-only false-safety budget). THREE, instanced GPU-resident geometry: borrow Cartograph_2.0 (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:31-95) with one InstancedStaticMesh or Niagara mesh per buildable class on a hidden MapMarkerActor; a buildable is one AddInstance scaled to its bounding box (GetBuildingBoundingBox via GetCombinedClearanceBox, 2.0 cpp:189-275); splines/wires/beams are thin oriented-box instances via get_line_transform (2.0 cpp:20-24); render via UMapCaptureComponent2D (ortho SceneCapture2D, GetViewOwner override plus ShowOnlyActorComponents(MapMarkerActor), CaptureSceneDeferred, 2.0 cpp:93-94); component count is bounded by classes (hundreds) not instances; add/remove is O(1) AddInstance/RemoveInstance not O(N) array shift plus O(N) redirector scan; capture cost is fixed regardless of changed-building count, killing the per-event CPU draw behind #14/#10. GLUE: the ISM/Niagara buffers ARE the GPU-resident render data, so CurrentBuildingData (h:359, ~344-432 B/building) and its precomputed FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache (~176 B derived) collapse to a slim map of classHash to ISM instance index for removal; on the host iterate AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem directly (already the gather source cpp:383-388). The GPU lens thus also pays the memory dividend.
designs.complexityBefore: Per build/remove event: O(N) redirector scan (cpp:1199-1205,1217-1230) + O(N) sorted-array Insert/RemoveAt memmove (cpp:575,597) on the game thread, then a redraw issuing a full-screen 8192x8192 opaque clear (256 MB write traffic on entire redraws) and, in a single GPU submission, rasterizing up to ~9N primitives (4 outline lines/rect + up to 8 lines/spline). For N=100k that is ~0.5-1M primitives in ONE render-thread flush (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:89). Under a build-drag, cancel/restart (cpp:442) throws away partial work so effective cost is (events/frame) times (full setup + clear). GPU work per submission is UNBOUNDED in N, hence TDR. Full redraw (Z-filter/layer) is O(N) draw with no culling (cpp:676-682). VRAM: fixed 256 MB.
designs.complexityAfter: Per build/remove event: O(1) AddInstance/RemoveInstance + O(k) tile-marking where k = tiles overlapped (typically 1-4). Per frame: GPU work is HARD-CAPPED at a configured primitive/tile budget B (e.g. 20k primitives or 8 tiles), so no single RHI submission exceeds B regardless of N, making the TDR structurally impossible. Localized redraw is O(buildings overlapping dirty tiles), not O(N). Persistent atlas means untouched tiles cost zero. With the instanced/SceneCapture path per-redraw cost is a fixed GPU capture of dirty tiles, roughly O(1) in changed-building count. VRAM: configurable; 4096x4096 = 64 MB (4x less) is a one-constant change, or tile-streaming keeps only occupied tiles resident.
dataStructures: TSet of FIntPoint DirtyTiles - coalesces per-event invalidations into discrete tiles popped under a per-frame budget; replaces the single-AABB FBox2D RedrawArea (h:374) whose union balloons across far-apart edits

Per-class TMap of uint32 classHash to UInstancedStaticMeshComponent (or Niagara per-type, as in Cartograph_2.0 NiagaraComponentPerType) on a hidden MapMarkerActor - GPU-resident instance buffers ARE the render data; component count bounded by ~hundreds of classes

TMap of BuildingId to FInstanceHandle (classHash, ISM instance index) for O(1) removal (RemoveInstance plus swap-back index fixup), replacing BuildingDataIndexRedirector (h:365) and TQuadTree of int32 (h:366) for the instanced path

Uniform spatial hash grid TMap of FIntPoint to TArray of BuildingId over the fixed world bounds (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH_BOUND h:28-31) keyed to tile size for the per-tile overlap query - O(1) insert/remove, O(cells) box query; replaces the quadtree+redirector lookup at cpp:686-708
UMapCaptureComponent2D (orthographic SceneCapture2D, GetViewOwner override) writing into the persistent UCanvasRenderTarget2D atlas, captured per dirty-tile rect under the per-frame budget
Reused ScissorArea std::array of 4 uint32 (h:375) and the FCartographCanvasRenderItem scissor path (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:104-105) for the scissored RHIClear in the canvas-fallback variant
designs.memoryImpact: VRAM: 8192x8192 RGBA8 = exactly 256 MB resident today (RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE h:35, RTF_RGBA8 uasset). Dropping RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE to 1024*4 quarters it to 64 MB (one-constant change; must match SizeX/SizeY in CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization.uasset; ORIGIN_UV/PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER h:37-38 are constexpr off it so transforms stay self-consistent). Tile-streaming (allocate only occupied tiles) drops empty/small saves far below 256 MB. RAM: the instanced path lets CurrentBuildingData (h:359, ~344-432 B/building, ~69-86 MB at 200k, ~344-432 MB at 1M) and the ~176 B/building precomputed DataCache collapse to ISM instance buffers (engine-managed ~80 B transform/instance, GPU-uploaded) plus a slim BuildingId-to-handle map (~12 B). Net RAM reduction at 1M buildings is hundreds of MB. The never-shrinking BuildingDataIndexRedirector leak (h:363, monotonic 4 B per lifetime-add) is eliminated because RemoveInstance frees the slot.
risks: SceneCapture2D of an ISM/Niagara marker layer needs isolation (GetViewOwner + ShowOnlyActorComponents, 2.0 cpp:93-94) so it ignores world lighting/fog/postprocess; matching the current per-category MainColor/OutlineColor look (cpp:794,805) needs an unlit material with per-instance color (PerInstanceCustomData) - non-trivial material work

Per-dirty-tile SceneCapture is not native (it renders its whole view); either keep one full ortho capture but bound its frequency/budget (simpler, still TDR-safe if the scene is cheap instanced geometry) or composite per-class ISM draws into the atlas via a custom RDG pass with a scissor (more RHI code). Start with the full-capture variant

Removing the global FCanvas GetBatchedElements hook (cpp:322-354), a process-wide tax on ALL canvases plus an unchecked static_cast hazard (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:342); the instanced/capture path makes it unnecessary, else gate the hook body on Canvas==CurrentCanvas

Per-frame budget plus multi-frame compositing makes updates progressive, not atomic; need a converged signal for the UI, and DirtyTiles must survive coroutine cancellation (do NOT clear them like RedrawArea at cpp:888-889) so build-drag progress is not thrown away
RemoveInstance on a UInstancedStaticMeshComponent swaps the last instance into the freed slot, so the BuildingId-to-index map must fix up the swapped instance (one extra O(1) update per remove)

Icon-type buildables with async texture load (cpp:755-758) do not map cleanly to instanced meshes; icons need a texture atlas in the marker material or stay on the canvas-fallback path; pre-resolve/pin icon textures before the draw loop either way

Dedicated server: SceneCapture/ISM render components must be client-only (the FPlatformProperties IsServerOnly guard exists at cpp:392,619); the server keeps only the authoritative data list for replication, so render-only structures must not move onto the server path (relevant to #9)
implementationSketch: Step 0 (one-line, immediate, low risk): reduce RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE from 1024*8 to 1024*4 (h:35) and match SizeX/SizeY in Content/UI/CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization.uasset; quarters VRAM 256 to 64 MB and quarters all clear/draw bandwidth; ORIGIN_UV/PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER (h:37-38) follow automatically

Step 1 (kills the TDR, medium risk, keeps current canvas pipeline): in RedrawMapCoroutine replace the full-screen opaque ClearItem (cpp:653-660) with a scissored RHIClear sized to ScissorArea (MinIntX/Y..MaxIntX/Y already computed at cpp:641-645) so partial redraws touch only the dirty rect; split the single flush into bounded passes by calling EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (cpp:901 path) + co_await NextTick + re-Begin (cpp:630) after every B primitives, so no RHI submission exceeds B; make B and the per-tile budget config (extend RedrawTimeBudget/InitializeTimeBudget at cpp:472)

Step 2 (persistent atlas + tiling): add TSet of FIntPoint DirtyTiles; in the build/remove lambdas (cpp:140,171,200) mark tiles overlapping the new building VisualBoxCache instead of accumulating RedrawArea; stop the full-clear path; per frame pop budgeted tiles, scissored-clear each, redraw only buildings overlapping it via a new uniform-grid query (replacing the quadtree+redirector path at cpp:686-708); do NOT clear DirtyTiles on coroutine cancel (contrast cpp:888-889) so build-drag progress is retained, removing the cancel/restart thrash behind #14 15s spikes

Step 3 (decouple ingestion from draw): change all five hooks (cpp:142,173,202,234,264) and the multicast path (CartographModSubsystem.cpp:46) to apply the O(1) data delta + mark dirty tiles immediately and request at most one budgeted draw pass per frame via a debounce flag instead of RedrawMap(false) cancel-restart (cpp:435-451); make OnZFilterUpdated (cpp:948) and OnLayerConfigChanged (cpp:411) mark ALL tiles dirty instead of forcing an immediate atomic O(N) entire redraw; add an explicit user-triggered full-redraw command (per #10) using the SetOpenMap input-context pattern from origin/show_buildable_ui

Step 4 (GPU-resident geometry, large, optional final): port Cartograph_2.0 MapMarkerActor + per-class ISM/Niagara (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:31-95, GetBuildingBoundingBox cpp:189-275, get_line_transform cpp:20-24) and UMapCaptureComponent2D (GetViewOwner + ShowOnlyActorComponents, CaptureSceneDeferred cpp:93-94); add/remove become AddInstance/RemoveInstance with a BuildingId-to-(classHash,instanceIndex) handle map; redraw becomes a budgeted CaptureSceneDeferred of the marker layer; delete CurrentBuildingData (h:359) and FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache, collapsing the RAM second-copy and the redirector leak; keep the canvas-fallback path for Icon-type buildables or move icons into a marker-material texture atlas

pick.chosenDesign: Design 1: chunked flush + scissored clear + persistent target. EndDraw+NextTick+BeginDraw in :714-885 bounds per-frame GPU; ~30 lines, no wire change.
pick.rationale: Single flush over the TDR is the crash. Redirector Remove writes -1 tombstones (:1224) never compacted, so cost drifts up (#14); gather :520-526 is O(N^2). Risk: 2nd BeginDraw must not clear the RT.
pick.mergedRecommendation: P0: chunk flush, scissor clear (:653-660), coalesce (:442), handle-map redirector (h:365), bulk-build (:520-526). P1: 1024*4 (256->64MB). P2: tiles (#10). P3: sparse store + grid.
pick.problem: One FCanvas, one GPU flush; budget (:556) paces emission not GPU, so a megabase exceeds the TDR into the 256MB target (h:35); client crashes (#14).

title: Make dedicated-server join robust (fix #9 crash) and scalable (transfer protocol + multicast strategy)

designs.designName: Hardened ping-pong RCO: null-safe Find, lifecycle cleanup, byte-driven completion, shared snapshot
designs.problem: Issue 9 join crash plus big-factory hang, all in CartographRemoteCallObject. Causes: unchecked deref-Find at RCO.cpp 65/73/87; no logout cleanup of the PlayerController-keyed map (RCO.h 88); int16 slice-count overflow past 67 MB (RCO.h 16/76/91, cpp 53/79/103); off-by-one slices and read-after-move (cpp 52-53); full 2047-byte sends leaking stack tail (cpp 17); per-join full serialize plus reliable-multicast flood (cpp 48, subsystem.h 32, module.cpp 927).
designs.lens: Minimal-diff surgical fixes that keep the current architecture but remove the worst crashes and leaks; low risk and shippable.
designs.approach: Keep the ping-pong protocol and transport; remove crashes/hangs without redesigning the wire format. PR1: (1) null-guard the three deref-Find sites (RCO.cpp 65/73/87) so timeout/Finished/rejoin races log-and-return instead of crashing, directly closing issue 9; (2) make the buffer a RAII uint8 TArray (RCO.h 15), serialize via a local writer then append, and delete both FMemory Free calls (cpp 67/88), killing double-free, shallow-move, and read-after-move; (3) add a Logout/EndPlay teardown (SUBSCRIBE near module.cpp 304-319) calling AbortTransferForPlayer (ClearTimer plus Remove), with a weak-pointer controller in the timeout lambda, stopping the buffer/timer leak; (4) byte-driven completion with int32 counts and a uint32 TotalByteSize (complete when received bytes reach it, cpp 103) and ceil-div slices (cpp 53), overflow-proof and move-trap-immune; (5) NetSerialize writes Size then only Size bytes (cpp 15-20), removing the stack-tail leak. PR2: serialize once into a shared ref-counted blob regenerated only on a dirty flag from OnBuildingDataAdd/Remove (one-over-N memory), and gate ClientUpdateBuildingData to skip Initial-phase clients and skip when empty.
designs.complexityBefore: Completion gated on int16 equality that wraps past about 67 MB or 32767 slices, so large factories never finish (unbounded). Per-join serialize order N held as one 3-15 MB copy per joiner. Crash probability per join nonzero, rising with size and joiners. Disconnect leaks one buffer plus timer, never reclaimed.
designs.complexityAfter: Per-join serialize still order N but completion correct for any N (int32 counts plus a byte-count test are overflow-proof). Crash probability about zero (Find null-guarded, weak-pointer timeout, single RAII owner). Disconnect leak zero (Logout/EndPlay reclaims). PR2 cuts per-join memory from N copies to one shared blob (one-over-N), no per-join realloc churn.

designs.memoryImpact: PR1 neutral-to-better; removes the per-leaving-player leak (one buffer up to tens of MB plus a timer) and stops sending about 2047 bytes of junk on tail slices. PR2 takes N joiners from N copies of 3-15 MB each (up to 30-60 MB spline-heavy) to one shared 3-15 MB blob, one-over-N, no per-join realloc churn.
risks: Logout hook target (GameMode Logout vs FGPlayerController EndPlay) must be the correct SML symbol and fire on timeout/seamless disconnects, not just clean leaves.
TArray switch requires removing BOTH FMemory Free sites (cpp 67/88) or it frees a TArray-owned pointer.

Widening counts plus adding TotalByteSize changes the RPC signature; client and server must update together or mixed-version joins desync.

PR2 multicast guard must replay builds between snapshot and Finished to the joiner or its map misses them.

designs.designName: Shared snapshot-blob streaming plus sequenced unreliable delta log
designs.lens: Best end-state transfer redesign; correctness and million-building scaling first
designs.approach: Replace per-player serialize-and-ping-pong with ONE shared immutable snapshot blob plus a sequenced delta log; join becomes a pull of generation and byte-offset. A: one shared TSharedRef blob built once per uint32 SnapshotGeneration (GameInstanceModule.cpp:916-932), shared by all joiners, deleting the per-player FBufferWriter and FMemory::Free (RCO.cpp:67,88) and the move-of-Archive bug (RCO.cpp:52-53). B: windowed pull by total bytes, 4-8 MTU slices per ack (RCO.h:33), complete on bytes-received (replaces RCO.cpp:103), counters uint32, only Size bytes sent (RCO.cpp:15-20). C: null-check every Find (RCO.cpp:65/73/87), key by PlayerState/NetId, RAII teardown on Logout/EndPlay so the join race retries. D: deltas become a sequenced UNRELIABLE multicast ring coalesced vs per batch (GameInstanceModule.cpp:927) plus a RELIABLE heartbeat; gaps pull or re-snapshot; in-Initial clients skipped.
designs.problem: Join issue 9 crashes. RCO.cpp:48 serializes ALL CurrentBuildingData per joiner; Find at RCO.cpp:65/73/87 unchecked, 10s timeout RCO.cpp:83-90 frees the entry so a late ack null-derefs. int64 Slices truncates to int16 (RCO.h:16,76,91); past 67MB completion RCO.cpp:103 never fires. NetSerialize sends fixed 2047 bytes RCO.cpp:15-20. ClientUpdateBuildingData is Reliable NetMulticast per batch (ModSubsystem.h:32).
designs.complexityBefore: Per join O(N) serialize plus O(N) memcpy per joiner. Transfer ~ceil N*20B/2047 reliable RPCs each one RTT (~2k at 200k, ~33k at the int16 ceiling). Delta one Reliable multicast per batch.
designs.complexityAfter: Snapshot O(N) once per generation shared, amortized O(1)/join. Transfer ~10-15x fewer RTTs, O(1) completion, no overflow. Delta O(1) append, one unreliable multicast per ~0.5-1s. Join-race crash eliminated.

designs.problem: Server join crashes from an unchecked lookup racing a timeout, overflows a slice counter, serializes the whole list per joiner, and floods reliable multicasts.
designs.designName: Shared instance snapshot blob with a GPU instanced client renderer
designs.lens: GPU and engine leveraging: off the game thread, off the CPU.
designs.approach: Wire format is per class instance transforms; the server shares one reference counted snapshot blob with all joiners; the client folds the stream into per class instanced components and renders one scene capture pass.
designs.complexityBefore: Order N serialize per joiner, allocation per joiner, overflow stall, crash per race; client redraw order N; live update order batch reliable multicast.
designs.complexityAfter: Snapshot once order N off thread, constant per player; no overflow; no crash; client constant time, one GPU pass; live updates constant time coalesced.

Per player blob handle, cursor, and timer keyed by a network id

designs.memoryImpact: One shared blob for all joiners with no double free; client instanced buffers replace the second full copy, its caches, and the quadtree, and the large CPU clear pass is gone.
risks: A scene capture adds rendering cost and a hidden actor, needs slim icon assets, and may not match the canvas look.
Off thread serialize needs worker safe reads and the unreliable scheme needs a resync state machine; as a fallback the join hardening alone fixes the crash.

Build or reuse one shared snapshot blob and stream slices to every joiner instead of one buffer per player.
Port the marker actor, instanced components, and scene capture, and apply records as add and remove instance calls, coalescing live deltas and skipping players still loading.

pick.problem: Dedicated-server join (issue #9 crash) is fragile and unscalable, all centered in CartographRemoteCallObject. Verified against source: (1) three unchecked map-Find derefs at RCO.cpp:65, :73, :87 (`*InitialBuildingDataToSendPerPlayer.Find(PlayerController)`) null-crash whenever a late ack, timeout, or rejoin races the per-player entry — this is the #9 crash. (2) The per-player map (RCO.h:88) and its timer have NO Logout/EndPlay teardown (module.cpp only SUBSCRIBEs build/remove/canvas hooks at :308-322), so a player who disconnects mid-transfer leaks one FBufferWriter buffer (up to tens of MB) plus a 10s timer permanently. (3) Slice completion overflows: `Slices` is int64 (RCO.h:16) but the RPC arg `TotalSliceCount` is int16 (RCO.h:76, cpp:94) and `ReceivedSliceCount` is int16 (RCO.h:91); with BuildingDataBufferMaxSize=2047 (RCO.h:33), the int16 counter wraps past 32767 slices ≈ 63 MB ≈ ~3.3M non-spline buildings, so big factories never complete the join. (4) Off-by-one slice count `TotalSize()/Max + 1` (cpp:53) always sends one extra/short slice; NetSerialize unconditionally serializes all 2047 bytes ignoring the actual `Size` (cpp:17), leaking stack-tail junk every slice. (5) Memory-safety hazards: `std::move(Archive)` at cpp:52 then read-after-move `Archive.TotalSize()` at cpp:53, plus manual `FMemory::Free(...GetWriterData())` at cpp:67 and :88 on a moved/owned buffer (FBufferWriter move is shallow). (6) Scalability: ServerRequestInitialBuildingData_Implementation (cpp:48) serializes ALL CurrentBuildingData per joiner into a fresh buffer (O(joiners*N) memory), and ClientUpdateBuildingData is NetMulticast+Reliable (ModSubsystem.h:32) fired every redraw at module.cpp:927 with no skip for empty payloads or for clients still in their Initial pull.
pick.chosenDesign: Design 1 — "Hardened ping-pong RCO: null-safe Find, lifecycle cleanup, byte-driven completion, shared snapshot" (the medium-effort, two-PR plan).
pick.rationale: Design 1 is the strongest PRIMARY because it is the only one whose root-cause mapping I could verify line-for-line against the source, and it fixes the actual shipped #9 crash (the three unchecked Finds at RCO.cpp:65/73/87) with minimal-diff surgical changes that keep the proven ping-pong transport and wire format. Its PR1 closes every confirmed defect — null-guard the Finds, RAII the buffer to kill the move/double-free trap (cpp:52-53/67/88), widen counters to int32 + byte-driven completion to kill the 63 MB overflow, ceil-div slices to kill the off-by-one, write only `Size` bytes to kill the stack-tail leak, and a Logout/EndPlay teardown to kill the disconnect leak — at low risk and shippable independently. Its PR2 (one shared ref-counted snapshot regenerated on a dirty flag, plus gating the multicast for in-Initial/empty clients) is the right next step and overlaps with the better parts of Designs 2 and 3 without their risk. Designs 2 and 3 (large effort) identify the same defects but propose simultaneously rewriting the transport to unreliable sequenced deltas (D2) or porting the entire client renderer to GPU instanced scene-capture (D3). Those are correct end-states for million-building scale but are far higher risk (unreliable-delta resync state machine; off-game-thread reads of CurrentBuildingData; a whole new rendering path with asset/visual-parity risk that D3 itself flags as possibly not matching the canvas look) and should not gate the crash fix. The merged plan below adopts Design 1 as the spine and grafts D2's windowed-pull + protocol-version-byte + generation number, deferring D3's GPU renderer as an optional long-term track.
pick.mergedRecommendation:
Ordered plan, crash-first then scale.

PHASE 0 — CRASH HOTFIX (ship alone, closes #9; ~1 day, surgical):
1. Null-guard all three derefs. At RCO.cpp:65, :73, :87 replace `*Find(PC)` with `auto* P = Find(PC); if (!P) { CARTO_LOG_WARNING(...); return; }`. This alone stops the #9 join crash on every late-ack / timeout / rejoin race.
2. Make the timeout lambda (cpp:83-90) capture a TWeakObjectPtr<APlayerController> and bail if invalid; have it null-guard its own Find before Remove. This stops the timer firing into a freed/absent entry.

PHASE 1 — MEMORY SAFETY + LEAK + OVERFLOW (Design 1 PR1; ~2-3 days):
3. Convert FInitialBuildingDataToSend.InitialBuildingData (RCO.h:15) from FBufferWriter-by-value to a RAII `TArray<uint8>`; add `uint32 TotalByteSize`. Serialize into a local FBufferWriter, append its bytes into the TArray, free the local writer once, then Add the struct. DELETE both `FMemory::Free(...GetWriterData())` at cpp:67 and :88 (TArray now owns the memory) — this removes the read-after-move (cpp:52-53) and double-free.
4. Set `Slices = ceil(TotalByteSize / Max)` not `/Max + 1` (cpp:53). Widen `Slices`, `ReceivedSliceCount`, and the RPC `TotalSliceCount` arg to int32; add a `uint32 TotalByteSize` RPC arg. Change completion (cpp:103) to byte-driven: complete when received-bytes >= TotalByteSize. Assert received never exceeds TotalByteSize. This is overflow-proof for any factory size.
5. In FBuildingDataBuffer::NetSerialize (cpp:15-20) serialize the actual Size first, then only Size bytes — kills the 2047-byte stack-tail leak per slice. (Add a Size field or pass it via the existing RPC `Size` param and serialize length-prefixed.)
6. Add a server-side teardown: SUBSCRIBE to the correct SML disconnect symbol near module.cpp:304 (verify GameMode::Logout vs FGPlayerController::EndPlay actually fires on timeout/seamless drops, not only clean leaves — this is the one real risk in PR1) calling an AbortTransferForPlayer(PC) that guards Find, ClearTimer, and Removes the entry. Kills the per-disconnect buffer+timer leak.
Note: changes 3-4 alter the RPC signature, so client and server must ship together; add a 1-byte protocol-version (grafted from Design 2) to the Initial handshake so mixed-version joins fail loudly instead of desyncing.

PHASE 2 — SCALABILITY (Design 1 PR2 + grafts from D2; ~3-5 days):
7. Shared snapshot (D1-PR2 / D2-A): replace the per-joiner serialize at cpp:48 with one `TSharedRef<const TArray<uint8>>` CachedSnapshot + `uint32 SnapshotGeneration`, regenerated only when a `bSnapshotDirty` flag is set by OnBuildingDataAdd (~module:1194) / OnBuildingDataRemove (~:1213). Each FInitialBuildingDataToSend holds a pinned ref to the snapshot + a uint32 byte-offset + generation it pinned. Cuts join memory from O(joiners*N) to O(N) (one ~4-15 MB blob for all joiners, no per-join realloc).
8. Windowed pull (graft D2-B): send 4-8 MTU-sized slices per client ack instead of 1, to cut the RTT count ~5-8x (a 200k-building join drops from ~2000 reliable round-trips to a few hundred). Keep the transport Reliable — do NOT adopt D2's unreliable-delta redesign yet; its resync state machine is the highest-risk piece and not needed to fix #9.
9. Gate the live multicast (module.cpp:927 / ModSubsystem.h:32): skip ClientUpdateBuildingData when both PendingAdd and PendingRemove are empty, and ensure builds that occur between snapshot capture and the joiner's Finished are replayed to that joiner (otherwise late joiners miss buildings — the explicit risk D1 flags). Simplest correct approach: capture snapshot generation at Initial, and after Finished the normal Reliable multicast already covers subsequent builds; the only gap to handle is builds during the pull, which the dirty-flag + generation pin makes detectable (re-pin or append a tail delta).

PHASE 3 — OPTIONAL LONG-TERM (Design 3, only if million-building scale is a real target): port the client to per-class InstancedStaticMesh components + a single SceneCapture pass, replacing the second full CPU copy, its caches, the BuildingDataIndexRedirector and CurrentBuildingQuadTree, and the full-screen CPU clear. High value for the separate memory/lag issues (#10/#14) but orthogonal to the join crash; do not couple it to this fix. Keep the hardened ping-pong as the fallback transport.
quickWins: Null-guard the three `*...Find(PlayerController)` derefs at RCO.cpp:65, :73, :87 — log-and-return on null. ~10 lines, closes the #9 join crash by itself.
Capture TWeakObjectPtr<APlayerController> in the timeout lambda (cpp:83-90) and null-guard its Find before Remove — stops the 10s timer crashing into a freed entry.
Fix the off-by-one slice count: `Slices = (TotalByteSize + Max - 1) / Max` instead of `TotalSize()/Max + 1` (cpp:53) — stops the always-extra/short trailing slice.
In NetSerialize (cpp:17) serialize only `Size` bytes, not the full 2047-byte fixed array — removes ~2 KB of stack-tail junk on every slice and shrinks total join bandwidth.

Gate ClientUpdateBuildingData at module.cpp:927 to skip when both PendingAddBuildingData and PendingRemoveBuildingData are empty — kills wasted Reliable NetMulticasts to every client on no-op redraws.

Delete both manual `FMemory::Free(...GetWriterData())` calls (cpp:67, :88) and let an owned buffer free itself — removes the double-free/read-after-move hazard from the shallow FBufferWriter move at cpp:52-53.

Widen the int16 slice counters (RCO.h:76 arg, :91 field) to int32 and switch completion (cpp:103) to a byte-count test — removes the ~63 MB / 32767-slice ceiling that makes large factories never finish joining.
